name: Mujaddara
blurb: Lebanese lentils and rice topped with deeply caramelized onions.
tip: Reducing the olive oil to 2–3 tbsp total would bring this closer to ~450 kcal.
method: Rinse the lentils and simmer in 2 cups water for about 15 minutes, until just tender but not mushy. Drain.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a wide pan. Add the sliced onions and cook slowly over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized — 20–25 minutes.
Remove half the caramelized onions and set aside as garnish.
Add the rice, cumin, coriander, and drained lentils to the pan with the remaining onions. Stir to coat.
Add 2 cups water or stock, season with salt, bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 15–18 minutes until the rice is tender.
Fluff with a fork, top with the reserved caramelized onions, and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Ratatouille
blurb: A rustic French Provençal vegetable stew.
tip: Already a fairly light dish — no major adjustment needed.
method: Heat olive oil in a large pot. Sauté the onion and garlic until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the eggplant and cook 5–6 minutes until it starts to soften, stirring occasionally.
Add the zucchini and bell peppers; cook another 5 minutes.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and herbs, and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer on low heat 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender and the stew has thickened.
Adjust seasoning and serve warm, with crusty bread or over rice.

name: Chiles Rellenos
blurb: Poblano peppers stuffed with melting cheese, battered and fried.
tip: Baking instead of shallow-frying meaningfully lowers the fat content — the oil absorption during frying is the biggest lever here.
ingredients: Monterey Jack cheese, cut into batons — 200 g
method: Char the poblano peppers over a flame or under a broiler until blackened all over. Steam in a covered bowl 10 minutes, then peel.
Make a slit in each pepper and remove the seeds, keeping the pepper whole. Stuff each with cheese batons.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks, then gently fold in the yolks to make a light batter.
Dredge the stuffed peppers in flour, then dip in the egg batter to coat.
Shallow-fry in hot oil, turning gently, until golden on all sides — about 3–4 minutes total.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with tomato sauce spooned over.

name: Gado-Gado
blurb: Indonesian vegetable salad with a rich peanut sauce.
tip: Using half the peanut sauce and topping up with a squeeze of extra lime keeps the dish bright while cutting calories.
ingredients: Mixed vegetables (green beans, cabbage, bean sprouts, carrots), blanched — 4 cups
Firm tofu, cubed and fried — 200 g
Kecap manis, or soy sauce + a little jaggery — 2 tbsp
Warm water — to thin the sauce
method: Blanch the mixed vegetables until just tender-crisp. Drain and cool.
Whisk the peanut butter, kecap manis, garlic, lime juice, and chili together with a little warm water into a smooth, pourable sauce.
Arrange the blanched vegetables, boiled potato, fried tofu, and cucumber on a plate.
Drizzle generously with the peanut sauce just before serving.
Serve at room temperature, with extra sauce on the side.

name: Misir Wat
blurb: A rich, spiced Ethiopian red lentil stew.
tip: Reducing the oil to 2 tbsp trims calories with little change to texture, since the lentils give the dish its body.
method: Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion until soft and golden, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the berbere spice and tomato paste; cook 1–2 minutes to deepen the flavor.
Add the rinsed red lentils and water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, 20–25 minutes until the lentils break down into a thick stew.
Season with salt and serve with injera or flatbread.

name: Miso Soup (Vegetarian Dashi)
blurb: A genuinely vegetarian miso soup, made with kombu dashi instead of the traditional bonito stock.
tip: Using silken tofu instead of firm brings this down to roughly 85 kcal/serving.
ingredients: White or yellow miso paste — 4 tbsp
method: Soak the kombu in the water for 20–30 minutes (or overnight, chilled) to make a vegetarian dashi.
Heat gently over low heat, removing the kombu just before it boils — boiling turns the stock bitter.
Add the rehydrated wakame and tofu cubes; keep at a gentle simmer.
Ladle a little hot dashi into a bowl, whisk in the miso paste until smooth, then stir it back into the pot. Don't let it boil after this.
Warm through gently without boiling.
Ladle into bowls, top with spring onions, and serve immediately.

name: Coconut Vegetable Curry (Thai-Style)
blurb: A base Thai green curry recipe, with notes for red and massaman variations.
tip: Swapping half the coconut milk for vegetable stock cuts roughly 100 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Mixed vegetables (eggplant, bell pepper, green beans, bamboo shoots) — 3 cups
Palm sugar or brown sugar — 1 tbsp
method: Scoop the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into a pot and heat until it starts to split and release its oil.
Add the curry paste and fry 2–3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the remaining coconut milk and stock; stir to combine.
Add the firmer vegetables first and simmer 5 minutes, then the tofu and remaining vegetables for another 5–7 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves; taste and adjust.
Finish with Thai basil just before serving, over steamed jasmine rice.

For red curry: swap in red curry paste, same method. For massaman: swap to massaman paste, add 2 cubed potatoes and 3 tbsp roasted peanuts, plus a cinnamon stick and 2 cardamom pods, simmering 20–25 minutes total.

name: Ta'ameya
blurb: Egyptian fava bean falafel, made from raw soaked beans rather than cooked chickpeas.
tip: Baking at 200°C (400°F) for about 20 minutes instead of deep-frying cuts roughly 100 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Dried split fava beans, soaked overnight — 1½ cups
method: Drain the soaked fava beans well — they're used raw, which is traditional for ta'ameya.
Blend the beans, onion, garlic, coriander, parsley, and dill until finely ground but not pureed.
Mix in the ground coriander, cumin, and salt; rest in the fridge 30 minutes.
Just before frying, mix in the baking soda.
Shape into patties, pressing sesame seeds onto both sides.
Deep-fry a few at a time until deep golden and crisp, about 3–4 minutes.
Drain and serve hot in flatbread with tahini sauce, tomatoes, and pickles.

name: Vegetable Tagine
blurb: A warmly spiced Moroccan stew of vegetables, chickpeas, and dried apricots.
tip: Leaving out the toasted almond garnish saves about 20 kcal/serving.
method: Heat the olive oil; sauté the onion until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and spices; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the carrots and cook 3–4 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, stock, and apricots; bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently 20 minutes, until the carrots begin to soften.
Add the zucchini, bell pepper, and chickpeas; simmer, covered, another 15–20 minutes until tender and thickened.
Season, garnish with coriander and almonds, and serve with couscous or flatbread.

name: Moqueca
blurb: A Brazilian coconut stew, vegetarian version with hearts of palm and tofu in place of fish.
tip: Using 'lite' coconut milk instead of full-fat cuts roughly 90 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Palm oil (dendê), or olive oil + a pinch of paprika — 2 tbsp
method: Heat the oil; sauté the onion and garlic until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the bell peppers and cook another 3–4 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook until they break down, about 5 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the hearts of palm and tofu; simmer 10–12 minutes.
Stir in lime juice, season, finish with coriander, and serve with white rice.

name: Paal Payasam
blurb: A South Indian rice and vermicelli kheer, gently spiced with cardamom.
tip: Using low-fat milk and reducing the sugar to ¼ cup brings this down to roughly 300 kcal/serving.
method: Heat the ghee; roast the cashews and raisins until golden and plump. Set aside.
Lightly roast the vermicelli in a little ghee until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Bring the milk to a gentle boil in a heavy-bottomed pot, then reduce to a simmer.
Add the roasted vermicelli; cook, stirring frequently, until soft, 8–10 minutes.
Add the sugar and cardamom powder; simmer another 5 minutes.
Stir in the roasted cashews and raisins. Serve warm or chilled.

name: Mysore Pak
blurb: A rich, ghee-heavy South Indian gram flour sweet — genuinely indulgent by tradition.
tip: Cutting the ghee to 1 cup and portioning into 12 pieces instead of 8 brings servings down to roughly 270 kcal.
method: Sieve the besan to remove lumps.
Combine sugar and water; boil to a one-string syrup consistency.
Melt the ghee separately and keep it warm.
Gradually whisk the besan into the syrup, stirring continuously.
Add the warm ghee a ladle at a time, stirring continuously, until the mixture thickens and turns porous.
Pour into a greased tray, spreading evenly. Cut into squares while still warm, then cool completely.

name: Horchata
blurb: A chilled Mexican rice and cinnamon beverage.
tip: Reducing the sugar to ¼ cup and skipping the added milk brings this to roughly 120 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Milk or plant milk (optional) — ½ cup
method: Combine the rice, 2 cups water, and cinnamon stick in a blender; blend briefly, then soak at least 4 hours (or overnight, chilled).
Blend the soaked mixture again until smooth.
Strain through a fine sieve or cheesecloth, pressing to extract as much liquid as possible.
Stir in the remaining water, sugar, vanilla, and milk if using.
Chill well and serve over ice.

name: Pad Thai (Vegetarian)
blurb: The classic Thai stir-fried noodle dish, made vegetarian.
tip: Omitting the eggs and reducing the oil to 2 tbsp brings this to roughly 420 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Palm sugar or brown sugar — 2 tbsp
method: Soak the noodles in warm water until pliable but still firm, 20–30 minutes; drain.
Whisk the tamarind paste, soy sauce, and sugar together for the sauce.
Heat the oil; fry the tofu until golden, then push to one side.
Add garlic, and scramble the eggs alongside if using.
Add the noodles and sauce; toss continuously until coated and just tender, 2–3 minutes.
Add the bean sprouts, carrot, and half the spring onions; toss another minute.
Top with peanuts and remaining spring onions, and serve with lime wedges.

name: Hummus & Za'atar Pita Platter
blurb: A shareable Middle Eastern hummus platter with warm za'atar pita.
tip: Serving 2 pitas instead of 4 as a lighter snack portion brings this to roughly 380 kcal/serving.
method: Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and salt until smooth, adding water as needed.
With the processor running, drizzle in 3 tbsp olive oil until light and creamy.
Warm the pita, brush lightly with the remaining olive oil, and sprinkle generously with za'atar.
Cut the pita into wedges.
Plate the hummus, drizzle with more olive oil, and serve with the pita wedges.

name: Vegetable Hakka Chow Mein
blurb: A quick, high-heat stir-fried noodle dish loaded with crisp vegetables.
tip: This dish is naturally light on protein — adding 150g cubed, pan-fried tofu makes it more filling for about +110 kcal and +11g protein.
method: Cook the noodles until just al dente; drain, toss with a little oil, and set aside.
Heat the oil; stir-fry the garlic and ginger briefly until fragrant.
Add the cabbage, carrot, and bell pepper; stir-fry on high heat 3–4 minutes, keeping them crisp.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, vinegar, and pepper; toss together on high heat 2–3 minutes.
Stir in most of the spring onions, garnish with the rest, and serve hot.

name: Brigadeiro
blurb: Brazilian chocolate fudge truffles, rolled in sprinkles.
tip: Treating this as a 1–2 truffle portion rather than 2–3 brings it to roughly 100–130 kcal.
method: Combine the condensed milk, cocoa powder, and butter in a saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens and pulls away from the pan sides, about 10–12 minutes.
Cool completely on a greased plate, about 1 hour.
Grease your hands lightly and roll into small balls.
Roll each ball in chocolate sprinkles. Serve in small paper cups, at room temperature.

name: Onigiri
blurb: Japanese filled rice balls, wrapped in nori.
tip: Already a light, low-fat snack — for a meal-sized portion, 3–4 onigiri brings it closer to 350–400 kcal.
ingredients: Japanese short-grain rice, cooked & lightly seasoned — 3 cups
Filling of choice (umeboshi, seasoned mushroom, or edamame + sesame) — ½ cup
method: Cook the rice and season lightly with rice vinegar if using; cool enough to handle.
Wet your hands and rub a little salt onto your palms.
Take a handful of rice, flatten slightly, and place a spoonful of filling in the center.
Fold the rice around the filling and shape into a triangle or ball, pressing firmly.
Wrap a strip of nori around the base of each onigiri.
Repeat with the remaining rice and filling. Serve at room temperature or slightly warm.

name: Harira
blurb: A warmly spiced Moroccan lentil and vegetable soup.
tip: Reducing the olive oil to 1 tbsp trims about 40 kcal/serving with little impact on flavor.
ingredients: Fresh coriander & parsley — ½ cup combined
method: Heat the olive oil; sauté the onion and celery until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the ginger, cinnamon, and turmeric; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste; cook 3–4 minutes.
Add the lentils, chickpeas, and stock; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, partially covered, 30–35 minutes until the lentils are tender.
For a thicker soup, whisk the flour with water and stir in, simmering 5 more minutes.
Stir in the fresh herbs just before serving, with lemon wedges.

name: Shiro Wat
blurb: A smooth, spiced Ethiopian chickpea flour stew.
tip: Reducing the oil to 2 tbsp cuts roughly 30 kcal/serving — the shiro itself gives the dish its body.
ingredients: Shiro powder (or chickpea flour + 1 tbsp berbere) — 1 cup
method: Heat the oil; sauté the onion until soft and golden, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and berbere spice; cook 1–2 minutes.
Whisk the shiro powder into the water separately until smooth and lump-free.
Gradually pour into the pot, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Simmer gently, stirring frequently, 15–20 minutes until thickened to a smooth, porridge-like consistency.
Season with salt and serve with injera or flatbread.

name: Pesarattu
blurb: A South Indian moong dal dosa, crisped with onion.
tip: Using 1 tsp oil per dosa on a well-seasoned pan instead of a generous drizzle saves about 60 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Whole green moong dal, soaked 4 hrs — 1½ cups
method: Drain the soaked moong dal and rice; blend with ginger, chilies, cumin, and a little water into a smooth, thick batter. Season with salt.
Heat a griddle, pour a ladle of batter, and spread into a thin circle.
Sprinkle chopped onion over the top and press gently; drizzle a little oil around the edges.
Cook until the base is golden and crisp, then flip briefly to finish.
Serve hot with coconut or ginger chutney.

name: Rasam
blurb: A light, tangy South Indian tamarind and lentil soup.
tip: Already very light; pair with a protein-rich side (like the Vada) for a balanced meal.
ingredients: Toor dal, cooked & mashed — ¼ cup
method: Soak tamarind in warm water, extract the pulp, and discard the fibers.
Combine the tamarind water, tomato, mashed dal, rasam powder, turmeric, and salt with the remaining water; simmer 10–12 minutes.
In a small pan, heat the ghee; add mustard seeds, cumin, curry leaves, and garlic, and let them sputter.
Pour this tempering over the simmering rasam.
Simmer 2–3 more minutes, garnish with coriander, and serve hot.

name: Vada (Medu Vada)
blurb: Crisp, fluffy South Indian lentil fritters.
tip: Baking or air-frying instead of deep-frying cuts roughly 150 kcal/serving.
method: Drain the soaked urad dal and grind to a thick, fluffy batter with minimal water.
Whisk the batter vigorously by hand for a few minutes to incorporate air.
Fold in the chilies, ginger, curry leaves, and pepper; season with salt.
Wet your hands and shape portions into donut-like rings.
Deep-fry until golden brown and crisp, turning occasionally.
Drain and serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.

name: Tom Yum Soup (Vegetarian)
blurb: A hot and sour Thai soup, fragrant with lemongrass and lime leaf.
tip: Add rice noodles for a more filling meal (+~150 kcal/serving) if serving as a main rather than a starter.
ingredients: Vegetarian chili paste (nam prik pao) — 2 tbsp
method: Bring the stock to a boil with the lemongrass, galangal, and lime leaves; simmer 5 minutes to infuse.
Add the mushrooms and tofu; simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the chili paste and soy sauce.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 2–3 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in the lime juice off the heat, to keep it bright.
Garnish with chilies and coriander; serve hot.

name: Fresh Vegetable Spring Rolls
blurb: Vietnamese-style fresh rice paper rolls with a peanut dipping sauce.
tip: Dip lightly rather than pouring the full sauce portion over — using half saves about 40 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Firm tofu, pan-fried and sliced — 200 g
Peanut dipping sauce (peanut butter, soy sauce, lime, water) — ½ cup
method: Arrange all filling ingredients within reach.
Dip a rice paper wrapper in warm water a few seconds until pliable.
Lay it flat; arrange lettuce, vermicelli, tofu, carrot, cucumber, and herbs in the lower third.
Fold the sides in and roll tightly from the bottom.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Whisk the dipping sauce ingredients together and serve alongside.

name: Nasi Goreng (Vegetarian)
blurb: Indonesian fried rice, topped with a fried egg.
tip: Omitting the fried egg topping brings this to roughly 440 kcal/serving.
method: Heat oil in a wok; fry the tofu until golden, then set aside.
Sauté shallots, garlic, and chili until fragrant.
Add the cold rice, breaking up clumps; stir-fry on high heat 3–4 minutes.
Add kecap manis and soy sauce; toss until evenly coated.
Return the tofu to the wok and toss through.
Fry the eggs separately if using, and top each serving with one.
Garnish with cucumber, tomato, and fried shallots.

name: Baba Ganoush
blurb: A smoky, creamy Middle Eastern eggplant dip.
tip: Reducing the finishing olive oil drizzle to 1 tbsp saves about 30 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Olive oil — 2 tbsp (plus more to serve)
method: Char the eggplants over a flame or under a broiler until blackened and soft inside, 15–20 minutes.
Cool slightly, peel off the skin, and drain excess liquid.
Mash or blend the flesh with tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and olive oil — a little texture is traditional.
Season with salt.
Drizzle with more olive oil and garnish with parsley. Serve with warm pita.

name: Fattoush Salad
blurb: A bright Levantine salad topped with crisp toasted pita.
tip: Reducing the olive oil to 2 tbsp and baking the pita instead of frying saves about 70 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Fresh mint & parsley — ½ cup combined
method: Toast or lightly fry the pita until crisp; break into bite-sized pieces.
Combine the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, onion, mint, and parsley in a large bowl.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, sumac, and salt for the dressing.
Toss the salad with the dressing just before serving.
Add the crisp pita last so it stays crunchy.

name: Kung Pao Tofu
blurb: A spicy, peanut-studded stir-fry, vegetarian take on the Sichuan classic.
tip: Cutting the peanuts to ⅓ cup and the oil to 2 tbsp brings this to roughly 300 kcal/serving.
method: Pan-fry the tofu in a little oil until golden on most sides; set aside.
Heat the remaining oil; add dried chilies, garlic, and ginger, stir-frying briefly.
Add the bell pepper and zucchini; stir-fry 3–4 minutes.
Whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, and the cornstarch slurry.
Return the tofu to the pan, pour in the sauce, and toss until thickened, about 2 minutes.
Stir in the peanuts and most of the spring onions; garnish with the rest and serve over rice.

name: Vegetable Fried Rice
blurb: A classic wok-fried rice, loaded with mixed vegetables.
tip: Omitting the eggs and using just 2 tbsp total oil brings this to roughly 350 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Mixed vegetables (carrot, peas, corn, beans) — 1½ cups
method: Heat vegetable oil in a wok; add garlic and stir-fry briefly.
Add the mixed vegetables and stir-fry 3–4 minutes.
If using eggs, push the vegetables aside, scramble the eggs, then mix together.
Add the cold rice, breaking up clumps; stir-fry on high heat 3–4 minutes.
Add soy sauce, sesame oil, and white pepper; toss to coat.
Stir in most of the spring onions, garnish with the rest, and serve hot.

name: Japanese Vegetable Tempura
blurb: Light, crisp battered and fried vegetables, served with a soy dipping sauce.
tip: Draining on a rack rather than paper towels (which reabsorb oil) and skipping the egg yolk saves about 40 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Mixed vegetables (sweet potato, eggplant, bell pepper, green beans), sliced — 4 cups
Tentsuyu dipping sauce (soy sauce, mirin, vegetarian dashi) — to serve
method: Prepare the dipping sauce by combining soy sauce, mirin, and vegetarian dashi.
Slice vegetables thin and even for quick, even cooking.
Just before frying, whisk the flour, ice-cold water, and egg yolk lightly — a few lumps are fine.
Heat oil to around 170–180°C (340–355°F).
Dip vegetable pieces in the batter and fry a few at a time until light golden and crisp, about 2 minutes.
Drain on a rack and serve immediately with the dipping sauce.

name: Chawanmushi
blurb: A silky Japanese savory egg custard, made with vegetarian dashi.
tip: Already minimal; no adjustment needed.
method: Whisk the eggs gently, avoiding too much air.
Combine with the cooled dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and salt; whisk gently, then strain for a silky texture.
Divide the mushrooms and spinach among 4 small heatproof cups.
Pour the egg mixture over, filling each cup about ¾ full.
Cover with foil and steam over gently simmering water 12–15 minutes, until just set with a slight wobble.
Serve warm, directly in the cups.

name: Zaalouk
blurb: A smoky Moroccan eggplant and tomato dip, warmed with cumin and paprika.
tip: Reducing the olive oil to 2 tbsp saves about 30 kcal/serving.
method: Heat olive oil; cook the diced eggplant over medium heat until softened, about 10 minutes.
Add garlic, cumin, and paprika; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes; cover and simmer 15–20 minutes, mashing occasionally, until soft and jam-like.
Stir in lemon juice and season with salt.
Finish with coriander and parsley; serve warm or at room temperature with bread.

name: Esquites
blurb: Mexican street corn salad, creamy and topped with cotija cheese.
tip: Swapping the mayonnaise for plain Greek yogurt cuts roughly 70 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Cotija or feta, crumbled — ½ cup
method: Heat the butter in a skillet; cook the corn, stirring, until lightly charred in spots, 8–10 minutes.
Cool slightly, then stir in the mayonnaise, half the cheese, lime juice, and chili powder.
Transfer to a bowl; top with remaining cheese, a little more chili powder, and coriander.
Serve warm or at room temperature with lime wedges.

name: Feijão Tropeiro (Vegetarian)
blurb: A Brazilian sauté of beans, greens, and toasted cassava flour.
tip: Omitting the boiled egg garnish saves about 40 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Cooked pinto or black beans — 2 cups
Collard greens or kale, shredded — 2 cups
method: Heat olive oil; sauté the onion and garlic until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the greens and cook until wilted, 3–4 minutes.
Stir in the smoked paprika, then add the beans; cook 5 minutes, lightly mashing a few to help everything bind.
Sprinkle in the cassava flour gradually, stirring constantly, until evenly toasted, 3–4 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Top with sliced hard-boiled egg if using, and serve warm.

name: Ful Medames
blurb: A classic Egyptian breakfast of warm, garlicky mashed fava beans.
tip: Reducing the olive oil to 2 tbsp saves about 25 kcal/serving.
method: Heat the fava beans with a little of their liquid; mash lightly, leaving some beans whole for texture.
Stir in garlic and cumin; warm through 5 minutes.
Off heat, stir in olive oil and lemon juice; season with salt.
Top with chopped tomato, onion, and parsley.
Serve warm with pita for scooping.

name: Congee (Vegetarian)
blurb: A comforting, thick Chinese rice porridge.
tip: Naturally very light — add a soft-boiled egg or tofu strips for a more filling, protein-rich breakfast (+~90 kcal, +8g protein).
ingredients: Toppings (pickled vegetables, fried shallots, tofu strips) — optional
method: Rinse the rice and combine with water/stock and ginger in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, 45–60 minutes, until it breaks down into a thick, creamy porridge.
Add more water if it thickens too much.
Season with soy sauce.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle with sesame oil, and top with spring onions and desired toppings.

name: Kinche
blurb: An Ethiopian savory cracked wheat porridge.
tip: Reducing the butter to 1 tbsp saves about 25 kcal/serving.
method: Rinse the cracked wheat.
Bring the water to a boil; add the wheat and a pinch of salt.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, 15–20 minutes, until thick and tender.
Stir in the butter and berbere spice if using.
Serve warm as a savory breakfast porridge.

name: Cong You Bing
blurb: Flaky, pan-fried Chinese scallion pancakes.
tip: Using less oil for pan-frying (1 tbsp per pancake) saves about 50 kcal/serving.
method: Gradually mix the boiling water into the flour to form a shaggy dough; knead smooth, then rest covered 30 minutes.
Divide into 4 portions; roll each into a thin circle.
Brush with sesame oil, sprinkle with salt and scallions, roll into a log, and coil into a spiral.
Flatten and roll out again into a thin round.
Pan-fry in a little oil until golden and crisp on both sides, 3–4 minutes per side.
Cut into wedges and serve hot.

name: Tamagoyaki
blurb: A gently sweet-savory Japanese rolled omelette.
tip: Already lean — no adjustment needed.
method: Whisk the eggs with dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar.
Heat a lightly oiled rectangular pan over medium heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg; when mostly set, roll it to one side.
Oil the empty pan space, pour in another thin layer letting it flow under the rolled portion, and continue rolling.
Repeat until all the egg is used, building layers into one roll.
Slice and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Pão de Queijo
blurb: Rich, chewy Brazilian cheese bread — genuinely indulgent by tradition.
tip: Reducing the oil to ¼ cup and using low-fat milk cuts roughly 150 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Parmesan or similar hard cheese, grated — 1 cup
method: Heat the milk, oil, and salt together until just simmering; pour over the tapioca starch and mix into a sticky dough.
Cool slightly, then knead in the eggs one at a time, followed by the cheese, until smooth and elastic.
Roll into small, golf-ball-sized portions.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 20–25 minutes, until puffed and golden.
Serve warm.

name: Sopa de Tortilla
blurb: A smoky Mexican tortilla soup, finished with avocado and crisp tortilla strips.
tip: Baking the tortilla strips instead of frying, and using half the avocado, saves about 70 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Queso fresco or feta, crumbled — ½ cup
method: Fry the tortilla strips in a little oil until crisp; drain and set aside.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic, and soaked chili until smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pot; cook the blended mixture 8–10 minutes until it darkens and thickens.
Add the stock; simmer 15 minutes. Season with salt.
Ladle into bowls, top with crispy tortilla strips, avocado, queso fresco, coriander, and lime.

name: Bissara
blurb: A creamy North African fava bean puree, drizzled with olive oil.
tip: Reducing the finishing olive oil to 1 tbsp total saves about 20 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Olive oil — 3 tbsp (plus more to serve)
method: Rinse the beans; combine with water and garlic in a pot.
Boil, then simmer 45–60 minutes until very soft and starting to break down.
Blend or mash until smooth, adding water as needed for a creamy, soup-like consistency.
Stir in cumin, olive oil, and salt.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle with more oil, sprinkle with paprika, and serve with lemon and bread.

name: Pongal
blurb: A comforting South Indian savory rice and lentil dish, tempered with cumin and pepper.
tip: Reducing the ghee to 2 tbsp saves about 30 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Split yellow moong dal — ½ cup
method: Dry-roast the moong dal lightly until fragrant, then rinse together with the rice.
Cook the rice and dal with water until very soft and porridge-like, about 20–25 minutes.
In a small pan, heat the ghee; add cumin, pepper, ginger, curry leaves, and cashews, sautéing until the cashews are golden.
Pour the tempering over the cooked rice and dal; mix well.
Season with salt; serve hot with coconut chutney or sambar.

name: Gomen
blurb: Ethiopian collard greens, slow-cooked until deeply tender.
tip: Reducing the oil to 2 tbsp saves about 25 kcal/serving.
method: Heat oil in a pot; sauté the onion until soft, cooking low and slow, 6–8 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and chili; cook 1–2 minutes.
Add the collard greens in batches, stirring to wilt.
Cover and cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, 20–25 minutes, until very tender.
Season with salt; serve with injera or flatbread.

name: Spanakopita
blurb: A crisp Greek spinach and feta pie, layered in phyllo.
tip: Reducing the brushing oil to 3 tbsp total saves about 60 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Olive oil — ¼ cup (for brushing + sauté)
method: Sauté the onion in a little olive oil until soft; add the spinach in batches and cook until wilted, then drain excess liquid.
Cool slightly, then mix with feta, eggs, and dill; season.
Layer half the phyllo in a baking dish, brushing each sheet lightly with oil.
Spread the spinach-feta filling evenly over the base.
Top with the remaining phyllo, brushing each layer, and score into portions.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 35–40 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool slightly before slicing.

name: Ethiopian Vegetable & Mushroom Tibs
blurb: A quick, high-heat Ethiopian mushroom and pepper stir-fry.
tip: Reducing the oil to 2 tbsp saves about 25 kcal/serving.
method: Heat oil in a wide pan over high heat; cook the onion until starting to soften, 3–4 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook until they release their liquid and start to brown, 5–6 minutes.
Add the bell peppers, garlic, and chili; stir-fry 4–5 minutes until tender but still with some bite.
Season with rosemary or berbere spice and salt.
Serve hot with injera or flatbread.

name: Arepas with Black Beans & Avocado
blurb: Grilled Colombian/Venezuelan cornmeal patties, filled with beans and avocado.
tip: Using a lighter hand with the avocado and queso fresco brings this to roughly 420 kcal/serving.
method: Mix the cornmeal with warm water and salt; rest 5 minutes until it forms a smooth, pliable dough.
Divide into 8 balls; flatten each into a disc about 1cm thick.
Cook on a lightly oiled griddle over medium heat, 5–7 minutes per side, until golden with a slight crust.
Split each arepa open slightly and fill with black beans, avocado, and queso fresco.
Garnish with coriander and serve warm.

name: Arroz con Leche
blurb: A creamy, cinnamon-scented Mexican rice pudding.
tip: Reducing the sugar to ⅓ cup and using low-fat milk brings this to roughly 340 kcal/serving.
method: Combine the rice, water, and cinnamon stick; boil, then simmer until the water is mostly absorbed, about 10 minutes.
Add the milk and sugar; simmer, stirring frequently, 25–30 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Stir in vanilla and raisins if using; remove the cinnamon stick.
Serve warm or chilled, dusted with ground cinnamon.

name: Karkade
blurb: A tart, ruby-red Egyptian hibiscus tea, served chilled.
tip: Can be enjoyed unsweetened for a virtually calorie-free option.
ingredients: Sugar or honey — 2–3 tbsp, to taste
method: Bring the water to a boil; add the dried hibiscus flowers.
Remove from heat, cover, and steep 10–15 minutes.
Strain out the flowers.
Stir in sugar or honey while still warm, so it dissolves easily.
Chill well and serve over ice, garnished with mint and lime.

name: Dal Tadka
blurb: Yellow lentil curry, finished with a sizzling cumin-garlic tempering.
tip: Reducing the ghee to 1 tbsp saves about 45 kcal/serving — the flavour is still strong.
method: Rinse the toor dal and pressure cook (or simmer) with water and turmeric until completely soft, about 20 minutes.
Heat ghee in a pan; add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add onion and cook until golden, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute, then add tomatoes and red chili powder.
Cook until the tomatoes break down, about 5 minutes.
Pour this tadka over the cooked dal; stir and simmer 5 minutes.
Season with salt, garnish with coriander, and serve with rice or roti.

name: Palak Paneer
blurb: Spinach and cottage cheese curry, silky and mildly spiced.
tip: Skipping the cream and using a splash of milk saves about 50 kcal/serving.
method: Blanch the spinach in boiling water 2 minutes; drain and blend to a smooth purée.
Pan-fry the paneer cubes until golden on two sides; set aside.
Heat oil; add cumin seeds, then onion, and cook until golden.
Add ginger, garlic, and green chilies; cook 1 minute.
Add the tomato and cook until soft; stir in the garam masala.
Add the spinach purée; simmer 5 minutes.
Fold in the paneer and cream; warm through and season with salt.

name: Aloo Paratha
blurb: Whole wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced mashed potato.
tip: Using just ½ tsp ghee per paratha instead of a generous knob saves about 60 kcal/serving.
method: Mix flour with water and salt; knead into a smooth dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Combine mashed potato, chilies, coriander, cumin, amchur, and salt for the filling.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Roll each into a small circle, place a spoonful of filling in the centre.
Gather the edges, pinch to seal, and gently roll out again into a flat disc.
Cook on a hot griddle with a little ghee, 2–3 minutes per side until golden.
Serve hot with yogurt and pickle.

name: Rajma Masala
blurb: Kidney bean curry in a deeply spiced onion-tomato gravy.
tip: Reducing the oil to 2 tbsp saves about 45 kcal/serving.
method: Heat oil; cook onion until deep golden, about 10 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add the puréed tomatoes and all spices; cook until oil separates, about 8 minutes.
Add the kidney beans and enough water to make a thick gravy.
Simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken.
Garnish with coriander; serve with steamed rice.

name: Chole
blurb: Spiced chickpea curry, sharp with chole masala and a squeeze of lemon.
tip: Already a lean dish — the oil is the main lever; 2 tbsp instead of 3 saves about 45 kcal.
method: Heat oil; add cumin seeds and bay leaf; let them splutter.
Add onion and cook until golden, about 8 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes and chole masala; cook until oil separates.
Add chickpeas and enough water for a thick gravy; simmer 15 minutes.
Squeeze in lemon juice, garnish with coriander, and serve with bhature or rice.

name: Matar Paneer
blurb: Peas and cottage cheese in a creamy cashew-tomato gravy.
tip: Skipping the cream and reducing cashews to 6 saves about 80 kcal/serving.
method: Blend the soaked cashews with a little water into a smooth paste; set aside.
Heat oil; add cumin seeds, then onion; cook until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 2 minutes.
Add puréed tomatoes and garam masala; cook until oil separates.
Stir in the cashew paste and cream; simmer 3 minutes.
Add peas and paneer; cook 5 minutes until heated through.
Season and serve with naan or roti.

name: Baingan Bharta
blurb: Smoky roasted aubergine mashed and simmered with onion and tomato.
tip: Already a very light dish — no real adjustment needed.
method: Char the aubergines directly over a flame or under a broiler until completely blackened. Cool, peel, and mash the flesh.
Heat oil; add cumin seeds, then onion; cook until golden, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and chili; cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and spices; cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the mashed aubergine; mix well and cook 8–10 minutes until the flavours meld.
Garnish with coriander; serve with roti.

name: Lassi
blurb: Chilled yogurt drink — sweet or salted, both ways refreshing.
tip: The salted version is naturally half the calories — a good everyday choice over the sweet.
ingredients: Sugar — 3 tbsp (sweet version) or Salt — ½ tsp (salted version)
Cardamom powder — ¼ tsp (sweet) or Cumin, roasted and ground — ½ tsp (salted)
method: For either version, blend all ingredients together until frothy and smooth.
Taste and adjust sweetness, salt, or spice.
Pour into glasses and serve immediately over ice.

name: Minestrone Soup
blurb: A hearty Italian vegetable and bean soup with small pasta.
tip: Halving the pasta and adding more beans keeps it filling at fewer carbs.
ingredients: Small pasta (ditalini or elbow) — ½ cup
method: Heat olive oil; sauté onion, carrots, and celery until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add garlic and oregano; cook 1 minute.
Add zucchini, tomatoes, beans, and stock; bring to a boil.
Add the pasta and simmer 10–12 minutes until pasta is just tender.
Season, garnish with fresh basil, and serve with crusty bread.

name: Caprese Salad with Burrata
blurb: Fresh tomato, basil, and burrata drizzled with olive oil and balsamic.
tip: Reducing the olive oil to 2 tbsp saves about 60 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Fresh basil leaves — a generous handful
method: Arrange tomato slices on a platter.
Tear or slice the burrata and place over the tomatoes.
Scatter the basil leaves generously.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic glaze.
Season with salt and cracked black pepper; serve immediately.

name: Lentil Soup
blurb: A French-style blended-and-chunky lentil soup, brightened with lemon.
tip: Reducing the olive oil to 2 tbsp saves about 45 kcal/serving.
method: Heat oil; sauté onion, carrots, and celery until soft, about 6 minutes.
Add garlic and thyme; cook 1 minute.
Add lentils, stock, and bay leaf; bring to a boil.
Simmer 25–30 minutes until lentils are completely tender.
Remove the bay leaf; blend half the soup for a creamy-chunky texture.
Stir in lemon juice, season, and serve with crusty bread.

name: Quiche Florentine
blurb: A spinach and cheese tart in a buttery pastry shell.
tip: Using half cream and half milk throughout saves about 60 kcal/serving.
method: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Spread the wilted, well-drained spinach evenly over the pastry base.
Scatter the grated cheese over the spinach.
Whisk together the eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Pour the custard over the spinach and cheese.
Bake 35–40 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the centre.
Cool 10 minutes before slicing; serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Potato Gratin
blurb: Thinly sliced potatoes baked in garlicky cream, French bistro style.
tip: Substituting half the cream with vegetable stock saves about 80 kcal/serving.
method: Preheat oven to 170°C (340°F). Rub a baking dish with the butter and garlic.
Warm the cream and milk together with garlic, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Layer the potato slices in the dish, pouring a little of the cream mixture over each layer.
Top with the remaining cream and scatter the cheese over.
Bake 55–60 minutes until the top is golden and the potatoes are completely tender.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.

name: Gazpacho
blurb: Chilled Spanish raw tomato and vegetable soup.
tip: Reducing the olive oil to 2 tbsp brings this to roughly 115 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Croutons and diced vegetables — to garnish
method: Roughly chop all the vegetables and blend until completely smooth.
Add the olive oil, vinegar, and salt; blend again.
Add ice-cold water to achieve a pourable soup consistency.
Pass through a sieve for a silky texture if preferred.
Chill at least 2 hours before serving.
Serve very cold, topped with croutons and finely diced cucumber, tomato, and pepper.

name: Bibimbap
blurb: Korean mixed rice bowl with sautéed vegetables, tofu, and gochujang.
tip: Halving the gochujang and using 1 tbsp sesame oil saves about 60 kcal/serving.
method: Prepare each vegetable topping separately: season spinach, carrots, and bean sprouts with a little sesame oil and soy sauce; sauté mushrooms with soy sauce.
Pan-fry the tofu until golden.
Divide the hot rice among 4 bowls.
Arrange the vegetable toppings and tofu in separate sections over the rice.
Top each bowl with a fried egg if using.
Add a spoonful of gochujang and a drizzle of sesame oil.
Mix everything together well at the table before eating.

name: Japchae
blurb: Korean glass noodles stir-fried with vegetables and sesame oil.
tip: Reducing the sesame oil to 1 tbsp and sugar to 1 tbsp saves about 80 kcal/serving.
method: Boil the glass noodles until tender (about 6 minutes); drain and cut into shorter lengths.
Toss noodles with 2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp sesame oil.
Stir-fry each vegetable separately in a little oil, seasoning with soy sauce.
Scramble the eggs separately if using.
Combine all the noodles, vegetables, and egg in a large pan; add the remaining soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil; toss together over medium heat.
Garnish with sesame seeds; serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Doenjang Jjigae
blurb: Korean fermented soybean paste stew with tofu and vegetables.
tip: Already very light — add tofu or an egg if you want more protein without significant extra calories.
method: Bring the dashi or water to a boil; stir in the doenjang paste until dissolved.
Add the onion, zucchini, and mushrooms; simmer 8 minutes.
Add the tofu and garlic; simmer another 5 minutes.
Add gochugaru if using; adjust seasoning.
Drizzle with sesame oil; garnish with spring onions.
Serve hot with steamed rice — the stew is salty enough to season the whole bowl.

name: Sundubu Jjigae
blurb: Soft tofu stew, spicy and comforting, optionally topped with an egg.
tip: Omitting the egg saves about 70 kcal/serving if a lighter portion is preferred.
method: Heat oil in an earthenware pot or saucepan; fry gochugaru 1 minute until fragrant.
Add garlic and onion; cook 2–3 minutes.
Pour in the stock; add mushrooms and zucchini; simmer 5 minutes.
Break in the silken tofu in large spoonfuls; simmer 3 minutes.
Crack an egg into the stew if using; cover and cook until just set.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil; garnish with spring onions.
Serve immediately with steamed rice.

name: Kimchi Bokkeumbap
blurb: Kimchi fried rice with crumbled tofu, topped with a fried egg.
tip: Omitting the fried egg and reducing gochujang to 1 tbsp brings this to roughly 350 kcal/serving.
method: Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat; stir-fry garlic 30 seconds.
Add the kimchi and crumbled tofu; stir-fry 3–4 minutes.
Add the rice, breaking up clumps; stir-fry 3–4 minutes on high heat.
Add gochujang, soy sauce, and sesame oil; toss to coat evenly.
Stir in most of the spring onions.
Top each serving with a fried egg if using; garnish with sesame seeds, nori strips, and remaining spring onions.

name: Sri Lankan Dal Curry (Parippu)
blurb: Red lentils simmered in coconut milk with a mustard-curry leaf tempering.
tip: Using light coconut milk instead of full-fat saves about 50 kcal/serving.
method: Cook the red lentils with water until soft; drain excess water.
Stir in coconut milk, turmeric, and salt; simmer 5 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan; fry mustard seeds and curry leaves until they splutter.
Add onion, garlic, ginger, and green chilies; cook until golden.
Pour this tempering over the lentils; stir and simmer 3 minutes.
Serve with steamed rice and other curries.

name: Kottu Roti (Vegetarian)
blurb: Sri Lankan chopped flatbread stir-fried with egg and vegetables.
tip: Reducing to 2 tbsp oil and using 2 eggs saves about 70 kcal/serving.
method: Heat oil in a wok; fry curry leaves until fragrant.
Add onion and cook until softened; add carrot, cabbage, and bell pepper; stir-fry 3–4 minutes.
Push vegetables to one side; scramble the eggs in the space alongside.
Add the chopped roti pieces; toss everything together on high heat.
Season with curry powder and soy sauce; stir-fry 3 more minutes.
Serve hot, ideally in the traditional loud-chopping style at the table.

name: Pol Sambol
blurb: Sri Lankan coconut relish, tangy and spicy — a table staple.
tip: Fresh grated coconut is naturally high in fat — a little goes a long way; half the serving still delivers the full flavour hit.
ingredients: Freshly grated coconut (or desiccated, soaked) — 1½ cups
Maldive fish substitute (dried shiitake powder, optional) — 1 tsp
method: Combine the grated coconut, red onion, and chilies in a bowl.
Add lime juice and salt; mix well, tasting as you go — it should be tangy and spicy.
Serve alongside rice, hoppers, or string hoppers as a side condiment.

name: Akara
blurb: Nigerian black-eyed pea fritters, light and airy inside, crisp outside.
tip: Baking at 200°C for 20 minutes, turning once, saves about 120 kcal/serving.
method: Drain and peel the soaked black-eyed peas by rubbing them between your palms; the skins will float off.
Blend the peeled peas, onion, and chilies with as little water as possible into a thick, smooth batter.
Whisk vigorously for several minutes to incorporate air — this makes the fritters light.
Season generously with salt.
Deep-fry spoonfuls in hot oil until golden and cooked through, about 3–4 minutes.
Drain and serve hot, with pap or a chili sauce alongside.

name: Jollof Rice (Vegetarian)
blurb: West Africa's iconic one-pot tomato rice, deeply savory and lightly spiced.
tip: Reducing the oil to 3 tbsp saves about 45 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Scotch bonnet or habanero chili — 1 (adjust to taste)
method: Blend the tomatoes, red pepper, and scotch bonnet into a smooth purée.
Heat oil in a heavy pot; fry onion until golden, about 6 minutes.
Add tomato paste and cook 2 minutes; add the blended tomato purée.
Cook the tomato base, stirring frequently, until darkened and the oil floats to the top — about 15 minutes.
Add the stock, bay leaves, and herbs; season with salt.
Rinse the rice and add to the pot; stir, cover tightly and cook on low heat 25 minutes.
Stir in the mixed vegetables; cover and steam 5 more minutes.

name: Egusi Soup (Vegetarian)
blurb: West African melon seed soup, rich with palm oil and leafy greens.
tip: Reducing palm oil to 2 tbsp saves about 55 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Spinach or bitter leaf, chopped — 3 cups
method: Heat the palm oil in a pot; fry onion until softened.
Add the blended tomatoes and pepper; cook 10 minutes until the oil rises.
Mix the ground egusi with a little water to form a paste; add to the pot in small lumps.
Cook the egusi, stirring, 10 minutes until it changes colour and is cooked through.
Add the stock, dried shiitake, and seasoning; simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the leafy greens; cook 3–4 minutes until wilted.
Serve with pounded yam, eba, or rice.

name: Dosa
blurb: Crisp South Indian rice-lentil crepe, served with chutney and sambar.
tip: Using ½ tsp oil per dosa on a non-stick griddle instead of a generous drizzle halves the fat contribution.
method: Soak rice, urad dal, and fenugreek seeds separately for 6–8 hours.
Grind together with water into a smooth, slightly thick batter.
Ferment at room temperature 8–12 hours until risen and slightly tangy.
Season with salt; the batter should pour easily.
Heat a griddle; pour a ladle of batter and spread in a thin circle.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges; cook until the base is golden and crisp.
Serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.

name: Coconut Chutney
blurb: Fresh coconut chutney with a mustard-curry leaf tempering.
tip: Already a light condiment — portion size is the main variable.
method: Blend coconut, green chilies, ginger, roasted chana dal, salt, and enough water into a smooth chutney.
Transfer to a bowl.
Heat coconut oil in a small pan; add mustard seeds and let them pop.
Add curry leaves and dried red chili; fry 30 seconds.
Pour this tempering over the chutney.
Serve alongside dosa, idli, or vada.

name: Avial
blurb: South Indian mixed vegetable curry in a coconut-yogurt sauce.
tip: Reducing the coconut oil to 1 tbsp saves about 55 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Mixed vegetables (yam, raw banana, drumstick, carrot, beans, raw mango) — 4 cups
method: Cook the mixed vegetables in a little water with turmeric and salt until just tender.
Grind coconut, green chilies, and cumin into a coarse paste.
Add the coconut paste to the cooked vegetables; stir and heat through.
Remove from heat; stir in the yogurt.
Heat coconut oil; fry curry leaves and pour over the avial.
Serve warm with rice or rice and dal.

name: Udon Noodle Soup
blurb: Thick udon noodles in a vegetarian kombu-dashi broth.
tip: Already a light meal — adding a soft-boiled egg adds ~70 kcal and +6g protein if a more filling bowl is wanted.
method: Prepare the kombu dashi by soaking kombu in cold water 30 minutes, then heating gently without boiling; remove kombu.
Season the dashi with soy sauce and mirin.
Cook the udon noodles according to packet instructions; drain.
Add mushrooms to the broth; simmer 5 minutes.
Divide noodles among bowls; ladle hot broth and mushrooms over.
Top with tofu slices, spring onions, and nori; drizzle with sesame oil.

name: Agedashi Tofu
blurb: Japanese crispy fried tofu served in a savory dashi broth.
tip: Pan-frying instead of deep-frying saves about 50 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Potato starch or cornstarch — ½ cup
method: Press the tofu between paper towels 20 minutes to remove moisture; cut into cubes.
Combine dashi, soy sauce, and mirin in a saucepan; warm gently.
Dredge the tofu cubes in potato starch to coat.
Deep-fry or pan-fry in hot oil until a crisp, light crust forms, about 2–3 minutes.
Drain and place in serving bowls.
Pour the warm broth over the tofu.
Top with grated daikon, spring onions, and ginger.

name: Korean Matcha Bingsu
blurb: Shaved matcha milk ice, topped with red bean paste and mochi.
tip: Using oat milk and halving the condensed milk keeps this around 130 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Red bean paste (anko, store-bought) — ½ cup
Drizzle of condensed milk — to serve
method: Whisk together the milk, condensed milk, and matcha until smooth.
Freeze in a shallow tray until solid, about 4 hours (or overnight).
Scrape or shave the frozen block into fine, fluffy ice crystals — a fork works; a blender pulse also works.
Pile the shaved ice into bowls.
Top with red bean paste, mochi pieces if using, and a drizzle of condensed milk.
Serve immediately.

name: Shakshuka
blurb: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce.
tip: Reducing the olive oil to 2 tbsp saves about 45 kcal/serving.
method: Heat olive oil in a wide pan; sauté onion and pepper until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and spices; cook 1 minute.
Crush in the tomatoes; simmer 15 minutes until thickened.
Make 6 wells in the sauce; crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook until the egg whites are just set but yolks are still runny, about 5–7 minutes.
Scatter with coriander and serve directly from the pan with bread.

name: Khachapuri
blurb: Georgian cheese bread shaped as a boat, topped with a runny egg.
tip: Using half the cheese and skipping the butter saves about 100 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Sulguni or feta mixed with mozzarella — 400g
method: Divide dough into 4; roll each into an oval shape.
Crumble the cheese and distribute over each oval, leaving a border.
Roll up the long edges to form a boat shape, pinching the ends.
Bake at 220°C (430°F) for 15 minutes until the dough is golden.
Remove from oven; make a small well in the cheese in each boat.
Crack one egg into each well; add a small knob of butter.
Return to the oven 3–4 minutes until the egg white is just set. Serve immediately.

name: Tabbouleh
blurb: A parsley-forward Levantine salad with bulgur, tomato, and lemon.
tip: Reducing the olive oil to 2 tbsp saves about 45 kcal/serving.
method: Pour boiling water over the bulgur (just enough to cover); cover and let it soak 15 minutes until absorbed. Fluff and cool.
The parsley is the star — chop it very finely.
Combine parsley, mint, tomatoes, and spring onions.
Add the cooled bulgur; dress with lemon juice and olive oil.
Season with salt; rest 30 minutes before serving for the flavours to develop.

name: Manakish
blurb: Lebanese flatbread topped with a fragrant za'atar and olive oil paste.
tip: Using 3 tbsp oil in the za'atar paste instead of 4 saves about 30 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Optional toppings: sliced tomato, cucumber, fresh mint, feta
method: Divide the dough into 4 balls; let rest 20 minutes.
Mix za'atar and olive oil into a thick paste.
Roll each ball into a thin round (~20cm).
Spread the za'atar paste generously over each round.
Bake in a very hot oven (250°C/480°F) or on a hot griddle 6–8 minutes until golden and slightly puffed.
Serve warm with fresh vegetables and optional feta alongside.

name: Muhammara
blurb: Roasted red pepper and walnut dip with pomegranate molasses.
tip: Reducing walnuts to ½ cup saves about 50 kcal/serving.
method: Roast or char the red peppers until blackened; peel, seed, and cool.
Toast the walnuts lightly in a dry pan.
Blend the peppers, walnuts, breadcrumbs, pomegranate molasses, cumin, chili, and lemon juice.
With the blender running, drizzle in the olive oil.
Taste; adjust heat and tartness with extra chili or molasses.
Serve with warm pita or flatbread; drizzle with oil and scatter a few whole walnuts on top.

name: Tacos de Frijoles
blurb: Mexican bean tacos with mashed avocado and salsa.
tip: Using just half the avocado saves about 80 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Pinto or black beans, cooked — 2 cups
Chipotle in adobo (or chili powder) — 1 tsp
Salsa or fresh tomato — ½ cup
method: Heat a little oil; fry onion and garlic until soft.
Add the beans, cumin, and chipotle; cook 5–8 minutes, mashing some beans to create a slightly chunky paste.
Warm the tortillas on a dry griddle.
Spread a little mashed avocado on each tortilla; add a spoonful of beans.
Top with salsa, crumbled cheese, and coriander.
Serve with lime wedges.

name: Agua Fresca de Jamaica
blurb: A tart Mexican hibiscus cooler, served over ice.
tip: Halving the sugar brings this to roughly 30 kcal/serving — still pleasantly tart.
method: Boil 2 cups water; steep the hibiscus flowers 10 minutes.
Strain the flowers; dissolve the sugar in the hot liquid.
Add the remaining 2 cups cold water and lime juice.
Chill well; serve over ice with fresh mint.

name: Elote
blurb: Mexican street corn on the cob, charred and dressed with mayo and cheese.
tip: Swapping mayo for Greek yogurt saves about 60 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Cotija or feta, crumbled — ½ cup
method: Grill or boil the corn until cooked and slightly charred, about 8–10 minutes.
While hot, brush each cob with mayonnaise.
Roll in or sprinkle with crumbled cheese.
Dust with chili powder and salt.
Serve immediately with lime wedges and coriander.

name: Ceviche de Coliflor
blurb: Peruvian cauliflower ceviche, bright with lime and ají amarillo.
tip: Already a very light dish — the main calorie variable is the accompaniment.
ingredients: Cauliflower, cut into small florets — 1 head
Ají amarillo paste (or orange chili) — 1 tbsp
Cancha (toasted corn) or tortilla chips — to serve
method: Lightly blanch the cauliflower florets 2–3 minutes; drain and cool.
Whisk together lime juice, ají amarillo paste, garlic, and salt.
Add the cauliflower, red onion, celery, and coriander; toss well.
Marinate 30 minutes — the lime juice will slightly "cook" the surfaces.
Serve with cancha or tortilla chips alongside.

name: Empanadas de Queso
blurb: Cheese-filled pastries with caramelized onion and olive.
tip: Using a lower-fat cheese and skipping the olives saves about 60 kcal/serving.
method: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Combine the grated cheese and caramelized onion.
Place a spoonful of filling and one olive (if using) on each dough disc.
Fold the dough over; crimp the edges firmly with a fork to seal.
Brush with beaten egg.
Bake 18–20 minutes until golden.
Cool slightly before serving — the filling is very hot.

name: Mapo Tofu (Vegetarian)
blurb: Sichuan-style silken tofu in a spicy, numbing bean-paste sauce.
tip: Using firm tofu instead of silken gives more structure and fewer calories — roughly 240 kcal/serving.
method: Cut the tofu into 2cm cubes; blanch briefly in lightly salted water; drain carefully.
Heat oil; fry the doubanjiang and fermented black beans 2 minutes until fragrant and the oil turns red.
Add garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute.
Add the stock; bring to a simmer.
Gently slide in the tofu; simmer 3–4 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken.
Finish with ground Sichuan pepper and sesame oil; garnish with spring onions. Serve over rice.

name: Dim Sum — Vegetable Steamed Dumplings
blurb: Har Gow-style steamed dumplings filled with cabbage, carrot, and mushroom.
tip: Already a naturally light dish — pan-frying the bases in a little oil (potsticker style) adds about 40 kcal/serving for a crisp texture.
ingredients: Dipping sauce (soy, vinegar, ginger) — to serve
method: Mix cabbage and carrot with a pinch of salt; squeeze out excess moisture.
Combine with mushrooms, spring onions, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, and cornstarch.
Place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each wrapper.
Moisten the edges and pleat/fold to seal.
Steam over boiling water 8–10 minutes until wrappers are translucent and filling is cooked.
Serve immediately with the dipping sauce.

name: Hot and Sour Soup (Vegetarian)
blurb: Classic Chinese soup, tangy with vinegar and laced with silky egg ribbons.
tip: Already a light soup — pairs well with a more substantial main dish.
method: Bring the stock to a boil; add mushrooms and bamboo shoots; simmer 5 minutes.
Add the tofu and soy sauce.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry gradually until the soup thickens.
Add the rice vinegar and white pepper — taste and adjust; it should be both hot and sour.
Slowly pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream while stirring to create egg ribbons.
Drizzle with sesame oil; garnish with spring onions.

name: Rendang Sayur
blurb: Indonesian vegetable rendang, slow-cooked in coconut milk until deeply dark.
tip: Using light coconut milk and reducing it by 25% saves about 80 kcal/serving.
ingredients: Jackfruit (young, canned) or mixed root vegetables — 600g
Kerisik (toasted coconut) or desiccated coconut — 3 tbsp
method: Blend shallots, garlic, chilies, galangal, and the ground spices into a paste.
Heat oil in a heavy pot; fry the spice paste until fragrant and darkened, about 5 minutes.
Add the jackfruit or vegetables, lemongrass, and lime leaves; stir to coat.
Add coconut milk; bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered on medium-low heat 40–45 minutes, stirring frequently, until the liquid reduces and the mixture turns dark and almost dry.
Stir in the kerisik; season with salt.
Serve with steamed rice.

name: Laksa (Vegetarian)
blurb: Malaysian coconut noodle soup with fried tofu and bean sprouts.
tip: Using light coconut milk and halving the laksa paste saves about 100 kcal/serving.
method: Soak rice noodles in hot water until pliable; drain.
Fry the laksa paste in a little oil 2–3 minutes until very fragrant.
Add stock and bring to a boil; add coconut milk and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the fried tofu; simmer 3 minutes.
Blanch the bean sprouts briefly in the broth.
Divide noodles among bowls; ladle over the hot broth.
Top with tofu, bean sprouts, spring onions, halved boiled egg if using, and herbs.
Serve with lime on the side.

name: Onam Sadya
blurb: A festival banana-leaf feast — the full Kerala Sadya, showcased as one entry.
tip: A full Sadya is a once-a-year festival meal, not calibrated against daily intake targets — documenting it honestly without adjusting the tradition.
ingredients: Parippu (green gram dal with coconut and ghee) — for rice course
Avial (mixed vegetable coconut curry) — 1 batch (see Avial)
Thoran (dry coconut-tempered vegetables) — beans, cabbage, or raw banana
Olan (white pumpkin and cowpeas in thin coconut milk) — 1 batch
Pulissery (ripe mango or cucumber in spiced yogurt curry) — 1 batch
Pachadi (pineapple or cucumber raita-style accompaniment) — 1 batch
Payasam (ada/rice and parippu/lentil, two types) — for dessert
method: Prepare each component separately over the course of the morning — Parippu, Avial, Thoran, Olan, Pulissery, and Pachadi.
Cook the two payasams last, since they hold well once made.
Wash and lay out banana leaves, tip pointing left, one per diner.
Arrange each dish in its traditional position on the leaf — pickle and pappadom near the front, curries along the sides, rice in the centre.
Serve rice with Parippu and ghee first, then work through the remaining dishes as the meal progresses.
Finish with both payasams, served last.

name: Pani Puri
blurb: Crisp hollow puris filled with spiced potato and dipped in tangy mint water.
tip: The pani itself adds almost nothing to the calorie count — most calories come from the fried puri shells.
method: Knead semolina and flour with water into a stiff dough; rest 20 minutes.
Roll very thin; cut into small circles (3–4 cm). Deep-fry until puffed and crisp.
Blend all pani ingredients (mint, coriander, chilies, tamarind, roasted cumin, black salt, sugar, water) until smooth; strain and chill.
Combine the potato filling with chickpeas and seasonings.
To serve, crack a small hole in each puri, fill with a spoonful of filling, and dip into the spiced pani just before eating.

name: Mole Verde
blurb: Oaxacan-style green mole sauce, complex and herby, served over vegetables.
tip: Reducing the pumpkin seeds to ⅓ cup saves about 50 kcal/serving — the flavour remains complex.
ingredients: Epazote or fresh herb mix — 2 tbsp
Mixed vegetables (zucchini, green beans, chayote) — 3 cups
method: Char the tomatillos and poblano peppers under a broiler until blistered; peel the peppers.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until they begin to pop.
Blend the tomatillos, peppers, toasted seeds, coriander, epazote, onion, and garlic into a smooth sauce.
Heat oil in a heavy pot; add the sauce all at once — it will sputter.
Fry the sauce, stirring constantly, 5–8 minutes until darkened and thickened.
Add the stock; simmer 20 minutes until the mole coats a spoon.
Add the mixed vegetables; cook until tender, 10–15 minutes.
Season with salt and cumin; serve over rice with warm tortillas.

name: Idli with Sambar & Chutney
blurb: Pillowy steamed rice cakes served with tangy sambar and cooling coconut chutney — the quintessential South Indian morning.
tip: Overnight batter stored in the fridge develops a pleasant tang and gives a lighter, more airy idli.
method: Steam idlis in a greased mould for 12–15 min until spongy.
Heat sambar in a small pan, adding a splash of water if too thick.
Prepare coconut chutney by blending fresh coconut, green chilli, ginger and tempering with mustard seeds.
Arrange idlis on a plate and drizzle ghee if using.
Serve with sambar in a bowl and chutney on the side.

name: Appam with Coconut Milk Stew
blurb: Lacy fermented rice crepes with crisp edges and a soft centre, paired with a fragrant, mild coconut milk vegetable stew.
tip: A teaspoon of coconut cream stirred into the stew just before serving adds richness without extra cooking.
method: Extract thick and thin coconut milk from grated coconut.
Cook potatoes, carrots and beans in thin coconut milk until tender.
Add thick coconut milk, green chillies, curry leaves and salt; simmer 5 min.
Heat appam pan; pour a ladle of batter, swirl to coat, cover and cook 2 min until edges crisp.
Serve hot appams alongside the warm coconut stew.

name: Rava Upma with Vegetables
blurb: A quick semolina porridge tempered with mustard seeds, curry leaves and crunchy cashews, studded with seasonal vegetables.
tip: Always add the rava to boiling water (not cold) and stir immediately to guarantee a lump-free upma.
ingredients: ½ cup mixed vegetables (peas, carrot, beans)
Salt and lemon juice to taste
method: Dry-roast semolina in a pan until fragrant and lightly golden; set aside.
Heat ghee, splutter mustard seeds and curry leaves, add cashews and fry until golden.
Add onion and sauté until translucent; add tomato and vegetables, cook 3 min.
Pour in 2 cups boiling water, add salt and stir in roasted semolina steadily.
Stir vigorously to prevent lumps, cover and cook 3 min; finish with lemon juice.

name: Kootu (Vegetable & Lentil Curry)
blurb: A thick, earthy South Indian curry of vegetables and chana dal bound with a freshly ground coconut paste — wholesome and deeply satisfying.
tip: Add the coconut paste at the end and simmer briefly — long cooking dulls its fresh flavour.
ingredients: 1 cup yam or raw banana, diced
½ cup chana dal, soaked 30 min
method: Pressure cook chana dal with a pinch of turmeric until soft but not mushy.
Boil yam or banana in salted water until just tender; drain.
Grind coconut, cumin, pepper and dried chillies to a smooth paste.
Combine cooked dal, vegetables and coconut paste; simmer 8 min until thick.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil; pour over and mix.

name: Kerala Vegetable Stew (Ishtoo)
blurb: A silky, mildly spiced coconut milk stew fragrant with whole spices — Kerala's answer to the Sunday comfort dish.
tip: Never boil after adding thick coconut milk — gentle heat keeps it silky and prevents curdling.
method: Heat coconut oil; add whole spices and sauté until fragrant.
Add onion, ginger and green chillies; cook until onion softens.
Add vegetables and thin coconut milk; simmer until vegetables are tender.
Pour in thick coconut milk and salt; heat gently without boiling.
Serve with appam or idiyappam.

name: Puliyodarai (Tamarind Rice)
blurb: Bold, tangy tamarind rice tempered with sesame oil and peanuts — a temple staple and beloved travel food.
tip: The tamarind paste can be made in bulk and refrigerated for a week — mix with hot rice anytime.
method: Soak tamarind in ½ cup warm water; squeeze and strain to extract pulp.
Heat sesame oil; splutter mustard seeds, chana dal, red chillies and curry leaves.
Add tamarind extract, turmeric and salt; cook until the paste thickens and oil separates.
Fold in cooked rice and peanuts; mix gently to coat every grain.
Rest 10 min before serving so the flavours meld.

name: Kadala Curry (Black Chickpea Curry)
blurb: Deep, robust Kerala-style black chickpea curry in a roasted coconut and spice gravy — the classic companion to Puttu.
tip: Roasting the coconut until amber rather than just pale gives the gravy its characteristic deep colour and nutty flavour.
method: Pressure cook soaked chickpeas with salt until tender (3–4 whistles).
Dry-roast grated coconut until golden; grind to a smooth paste.
Sauté onions until deep golden; add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes and spice powders.
Add cooked chickpeas and coconut paste; simmer 10 min until gravy thickens.
Finish with coconut oil tempering of mustard seeds and curry leaves.

name: Masala Bajji (Vegetable Fritters)
blurb: Crisp gram-flour fritters with a spiced vegetable filling — the quintessential South Indian rainy-day snack.
tip: A pinch of baking soda in the batter gives a lighter, crisper crust.
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes or 1 raw banana, sliced
method: Whisk gram flour with chilli, turmeric, ajwain, salt and enough water to make a thick batter.
Heat oil to 175°C.
Dip vegetable slices into batter, coating evenly.
Fry in batches until golden and crisp, about 3–4 min per side.
Drain on paper and serve hot with coconut chutney.

name: Paniyaram
blurb: Crispy-outside, fluffy-inside dumplings made from fermented rice batter, cooked in a special mould — a clever way to use leftover dosa batter.
tip: Keep the heat at medium-low after adding the batter — too high and the outside burns before the centre cooks through.
ingredients: 1 tsp oil plus oil for greasing
method: Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil; add onion, chilli and coconut; sauté 3 min.
Stir tempered mix into the batter.
Heat a paniyaram mould; grease each cavity with a drop of oil.
Fill each cavity ¾ full; cover and cook on medium heat 4 min until base is golden.
Flip with a skewer and cook 2 min more; serve with tomato chutney.

name: Sundal (Spiced Chickpeas)
blurb: A light, protein-rich South Indian stir-fry of boiled legumes tempered with coconut and spices — a Navratri staple and everyday snack.
tip: Works equally well with black-eyed peas, kidney beans or cooked corn — use whatever legume you have.
ingredients: Salt and lime juice to taste
method: Heat oil; splutter mustard seeds, dried chilli and curry leaves.
Add asafoetida, then chickpeas; toss well to coat in the tempering.
Add salt and coconut; stir-fry 2 min on high heat.
Finish with a squeeze of lime juice.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Poha (Flattened Rice Stir-Fry)
blurb: Light, golden and fragrant — this central-Indian breakfast of flattened rice tossed with mustard seeds, peanuts and a squeeze of lemon never disappoints.
tip: Rinsing just until soft and draining immediately keeps each flake separate rather than mushy.
ingredients: Lemon juice and coriander to finish
method: Rinse poha under cold water until just soft; drain and set aside — do not over-soak.
Heat oil; splutter mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Add onion and chillies; sauté until onion softens.
Add turmeric, sugar and peanuts; toss well, then fold in poha.
Season with salt and lemon juice; garnish with coriander and serve.

name: Besan Chilla (Gram Flour Crepe)
blurb: A protein-packed savoury crepe made from spiced gram flour — quicker than a dosa, just as satisfying.
tip: Resting the batter 5 min after mixing allows the flour to hydrate and the chilla to cook more evenly.
method: Whisk gram flour with all vegetables, spices and salt; add water to make a pourable batter.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat; brush with a little oil.
Pour a ladleful of batter and spread into a thin circle.
Drizzle oil around edges; cook 2–3 min until edges lift, then flip and cook 1 min.
Serve immediately with mint chutney or pickled onions.

name: Sabudana Khichdi
blurb: Soft, chewy tapioca pearls tossed with roasted peanuts, green chillies and cumin — a popular fasting dish that doubles as a perfect weekend breakfast.
tip: The key is the right soak: pearls should be just separate and non-sticky — neither crunchy nor a paste.
ingredients: ½ cup roasted peanuts, coarsely crushed
method: Soak sabudana in just enough water to cover for 4–6 hours; drain and fluff with a fork.
Heat ghee; splutter cumin seeds, then add chillies and potatoes; toss 3 min.
Add sabudana and peanuts; fold gently to avoid breaking the pearls.
Cook uncovered 5 min, stirring occasionally, until pearls turn translucent.
Season with salt, sugar and lemon juice; garnish with coriander.

name: Methi Thepla
blurb: Thin, pliable Gujarati flatbreads enriched with fresh fenugreek leaves and yoghurt — perfect for breakfast or packed for travel.
tip: Theplas stay soft for 2–3 days when stored between layers of foil — ideal for packed lunches.
ingredients: ½ cup fresh methi (fenugreek) leaves, chopped
method: Mix all ingredients except oil with enough water to form a soft, pliable dough; rest 10 min.
Divide into equal balls; roll each out thinly.
Heat a tawa over medium-high heat; cook thepla 1 min per side, pressing lightly.
Apply a thin smear of oil; flip and cook until golden spots appear.
Serve with yoghurt, mango pickle or green chutney.

name: Kadhi Pakora
blurb: Tangy yoghurt-based gravy with gram flour dumplings — a North Indian comfort classic that tastes better the next day.
tip: Constant stirring during the first 15 minutes of cooking prevents the yoghurt from splitting.
ingredients: For pakoras: ½ cup besan, 1 onion sliced
Tempering: ghee, cumin, dried chilli, mustard seeds, hing
method: Whisk yoghurt, besan, turmeric, chilli and salt into a smooth batter; thin with 2 cups water.
Cook yoghurt mixture on medium heat, stirring constantly, for 20 min until thick.
Mix onion pakora batter; drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry until golden; drain.
Add pakoras to the kadhi; simmer 8 min so they soak up the gravy.
Finish with a sizzling tempering of ghee, cumin, mustard seeds and dried chilli poured over the top.

name: Vegetable Biryani
blurb: Fragrant basmati rice layered with spiced vegetables, caramelised onions and saffron milk — a celebratory one-pot that is worth every minute.
tip: Parboiling rice to exactly 70% cooked is the secret — it finishes on dum without going mushy.
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (carrot, peas, potato, beans)
1 tsp saffron in 3 tbsp warm milk
Whole spices: cloves, cardamom, bay leaf
method: Fry onions in ghee until deep golden and crisp; drain (these are fried onions for topping).
Marinate vegetables in yoghurt, biryani masala, chilli and ginger-garlic paste for 15 min.
Parboil soaked rice with whole spices and salt until 70% cooked; drain.
Layer marinated vegetables then rice in a heavy pot; top with fried onions, saffron milk, mint and ghee.
Seal and cook on dum (very low heat) for 20 min; rest 5 min before opening.

name: Dal Makhani
blurb: Slow-simmered whole black lentils in a rich, buttery tomato gravy — the signature dish of the North Indian restaurant tradition.
tip: Restaurant-quality dal makhani comes from slow simmering for an hour or more — do not rush this step.
method: Soak lentils and rajma overnight; pressure cook until very soft (6–7 whistles).
Mash slightly with the back of a spoon while still in the cooker.
Heat butter; add ginger-garlic paste, then tomato purée; cook until oil surfaces.
Add cooked dal, chilli powder, salt and 1 cup water; simmer 30 min, stirring often.
Stir in cream and garam masala; cook 5 more min and serve with naan.

name: Shahi Paneer
blurb: Cubes of fresh cottage cheese bathed in a regal cashew and cream gravy perfumed with cardamom — rich, mild and deeply satisfying.
tip: Soaking cashews for 30 min before blending gives a silkier, creamier sauce with no grit.
method: Boil onions and cashews together for 10 min; blend to a smooth paste.
Heat ghee; add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 min.
Add tomato and cook until soft; blend this too, combine with cashew-onion paste.
Return gravy to pan; add chilli, cardamom, salt and simmer 10 min.
Add paneer and cream; heat 3 min and garnish with cream swirl and dried rose petals.

name: Aloo Tikki Chaat
blurb: Crispy spiced potato patties smothered in yoghurt, tamarind chutney and pomegranate — the street-food dish that defines Delhi evenings.
tip: Frying in a well-oiled pan on medium-low gives a crust that stays crisp even after topping.
ingredients: Sev, pomegranate seeds and coriander to top
method: Mix mashed potato with salt, cumin and chaat masala; shape into flat patties.
Shallow-fry on medium heat until deeply golden and crisp on both sides.
Place patties on a plate; top with warm chickpeas.
Drizzle cold yoghurt, tamarind and green chutneys liberally.
Finish with sev, pomegranate and coriander; serve immediately.

name: Samosa with Mint Chutney
blurb: Flaky triangular pastry filled with spiced mashed potato and peas — perhaps the most universally beloved Indian snack.
tip: Frying on medium rather than high heat ensures the pastry cooks through and turns properly flaky.
ingredients: For pastry: 1 cup flour, 2 tbsp oil, salt, water
For filling: 3 potatoes boiled, ½ cup peas
1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp coriander powder
½ tsp amchur, 1 green chilli minced
method: Make a stiff pastry dough with flour, oil and salt; rest 20 min.
Sauté cumin, chilli and peas; add mashed potato, amchur and coriander; cool.
Roll pastry thin; cut into semi-circles; fold into cones, fill and seal with water.
Deep fry on medium heat (not high) until golden — about 8–10 min.
Drain and serve with fresh mint chutney.

name: Dahi Bhalla
blurb: Soft, spongy lentil dumplings soaked in cold yoghurt and topped with tamarind and green chutneys — a cooling contrast of textures and temperatures.
tip: Soaking the fried bhallas in water is non-negotiable — it makes them impossibly soft and helps them absorb the yoghurt.
ingredients: 1 cup thick yoghurt, whisked and sweetened
Cumin powder and chaat masala to dust
Fresh coriander and pomegranate to garnish
method: Grind soaked dal to a fluffy batter; whisk vigorously to incorporate air.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry until light golden; do not over-fry.
Soak fried bhallas in warm salted water for 10 min; squeeze gently and place on plate.
Pour chilled yoghurt over generously; drizzle both chutneys.
Dust with cumin and chaat masala; garnish and serve cold.

name: Bhel Puri
blurb: The iconic Mumbai street snack — puffed rice tossed with crunchy sev, raw mango, onion and two chutneys in a brisk, textured salad.
tip: Mix and serve instantly — bhel turns soggy within minutes of adding chutney.
method: Combine puffed rice, onion, potato and raw mango in a large bowl.
Add both chutneys and chaat masala; toss briskly.
Fold in sev last, tossing just once to keep it crunchy.
Transfer immediately to serving bowls.
Garnish with coriander and serve within 2 minutes.

name: Nasi Lemak (Vegetarian)
blurb: Coconut-fragrant rice with crispy peanuts, cucumber, boiled egg and a fiery sambal â€” Malaysia's national breakfast, vegetarian style.
tip: Pressing a piece of pandan leaf into the rice cooker is the single step that transforms plain coconut rice into something aromatic.
ingredients: 1 cup jasmine rice cooked in coconut milk with pandan leaf
Sambal: 5 dried chillies, 1 onion, 1 tomato, tamarind, sugar, salt
method: Cook rinsed rice in equal parts coconut milk and water with pandan leaf and salt.
Blend sambal ingredients and fry in oil until deep red and fragrant, about 10 min.
Halve hard-boiled eggs.
Arrange rice on a plate; place peanuts, cucumber and egg alongside.
Spoon sambal generously and serve.

name: Khao Tom (Thai Rice Porridge)
blurb: Silky, mild Thai rice soup garnished with ginger, spring onion and crispy garlic â€” the soothing blank canvas of Southeast Asian mornings.
tip: Cooking the rice in stock rather than water gives depth without any extra effort.
method: Simmer rice in stock with ginger on medium heat for 20 min, stirring occasionally, until porridge-like.
Season with soy sauce, sesame oil and white pepper.
Ladle into bowls; top with spring onion, fried garlic and coriander.
Serve with a wedge of lime and sliced chilli on the side.
Add a soft-boiled egg for extra protein.

name: Roti Canai with Vegetable Dal
blurb: Flaky, layered Malaysian flatbread served with a yellow lentil dal â€” the morning ritual of a region.
tip: The dough must rest fully so the gluten relaxes enough to stretch tissue-thin without tearing.
ingredients: For roti: 2 cups plain flour, 1 egg, 2 tbsp condensed milk, salt, ghee
For dal: 1/2 cup red lentils, 1 onion, 1 tomato
Coconut milk splash, curry leaves, mustard seeds
method: Mix flour, egg, condensed milk and salt into a soft dough; rest 30 min, divide into balls.
Stretch each ball on an oiled surface into a paper-thin sheet; fold into a square.
Cook on a hot iron griddle with ghee until golden and puffed; crumple gently to flake.
Simmer red lentils with onion, tomato, curry powder and turmeric until soft; thin with coconut milk.
Serve roti with warm dal on the side.

name: Jok (Thai Congee with Tofu)
blurb: Warming Thai rice porridge with silken tofu, fresh ginger and crispy fried shallots.
tip: Stirring vigorously halfway through breaks the grains slightly and gives a naturally creamier congee.
