ingredients: White pepper and sesame oil to taste
method: Simmer rice in stock, stirring often, for 20-25 min until very soft and creamy.
Gently slide in tofu cubes and warm through 2 min.
Season with soy sauce and white pepper.
Ladle into bowls; top with fried shallots, ginger and spring onion.
Finish with a few drops of sesame oil.

name: Mee Goreng Breakfast
blurb: Spiced fried egg noodles with tofu and bean sprouts, sauced with soy and chilli â€” a fast, fiery Southeast Asian morning.
tip: A very hot wok is non-negotiable â€” the smoky char is what separates good mee goreng from great.
ingredients: 2 spring onions and lime to serve
method: Heat oil in a wok over high heat; fry tofu until golden, push to the side.
Add garlic and onion; stir-fry 1 min, then push aside and scramble eggs.
Add noodles and toss everything together vigorously.
Pour in kecap manis and chilli sauce; toss 2 min on high heat.
Add bean sprouts, toss 30 seconds and serve with spring onion and lime.

name: Banh Mi Chay (Vegetarian Baguette)
blurb: A Vietnamese vegetarian baguette stuffed with lemongrass tofu, pickled daikon, cucumber and fresh herbs â€” an explosion of textures.
tip: Start the pickled daikon and carrot the evening before â€” even a 30-minute pickle makes a difference.
ingredients: 150g firm tofu, sliced and marinated in lemongrass, soy and sugar
1/2 cup pickled daikon and carrot (in vinegar and sugar)
Fresh coriander, mint and sliced chilli
method: Pan-fry marinated tofu until caramelised on both sides.
Split baguettes and toast lightly inside.
Spread mayo; drizzle a few drops of Maggi sauce.
Layer with tofu, pickled vegetables, cucumber and herbs.
Top with sliced chilli and serve immediately.

name: Pho Chay (Vegetarian Noodle Soup)
blurb: A clear, deeply aromatic Vietnamese broth scented with charred ginger and star anise, poured over rice noodles and fresh herbs.
tip: Charring the onion and ginger directly on a flame adds the subtle smokiness that defines an authentic pho broth.
ingredients: 1 large onion, halved and charred on flame
Bean sprouts, Thai basil, lime, sliced chilli to serve
Hoisin and sriracha on the side
method: Toast spices in a dry pan until fragrant; add to stock with charred onion and ginger.
Simmer broth 30 min; strain and season with soy sauce and salt.
Soak rice noodles per packet; blanch bean sprouts briefly.
Divide noodles into bowls; ladle hot broth over.
Serve immediately with herb plate and condiments.

name: Char Kway Teow (Vegetarian)
blurb: Smoky, chewy flat rice noodles stir-fried at blistering heat with egg, bean sprouts and soy â€” the street-food legend of Penang.
tip: Let noodles sit for a few seconds before tossing â€” that rest develops the wok char.
method: Heat wok to smoking point with oil; fry garlic until golden.
Add noodles and toss vigorously for 1 min.
Push noodles aside; scramble eggs in the gap, then fold into noodles.
Add soy sauces and chilli paste; toss on high heat 2 min.
Add bean sprouts and spring onion; toss 30 seconds and serve.

name: Mango Sticky Rice
blurb: Sweet glutinous rice bathed in salted coconut milk alongside ripe mango â€” Thailand's most beloved dessert-snack.
tip: Resist lifting the lid during the 15-minute rest â€” the rice soaks up all the coconut milk undisturbed.
method: Steam soaked glutinous rice for 20-25 min until translucent.
Warm coconut milk with sugar and salt until dissolved; do not boil.
Pour two-thirds of the coconut sauce over hot rice; stir and cover for 15 min to absorb.
Slice mango and arrange alongside rice.
Drizzle remaining coconut cream and scatter sesame seeds.

name: Banh Trang Nuong (Vietnamese Grilled Rice Paper)
blurb: Crispy grilled rice paper spread with egg, spring onion and chilli sauce â€” Da Lat's famous street snack, simple and addictive.
tip: Work fast â€” the rice paper crisps within seconds and the egg sets quickly over direct heat.
method: Place a rice paper sheet directly on a wire rack over a gas flame or in a dry pan.
When it starts to blister, brush one side with a little butter.
Crack half an egg over the sheet; spread gently with a spoon.
Scatter spring onion and drizzle soy and chilli sauce.
Cook until egg sets; fold in half and eat immediately while crisp.

name: Satay Tofu with Peanut Sauce
blurb: Skewered tofu grilled with lemongrass marinade and served with a rich, creamy peanut sauce.
tip: Press tofu for at least 20 minutes before marinating so it absorbs flavour instead of releasing water.
ingredients: Marinade: 1 stalk lemongrass minced, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp curry powder, soy sauce
Peanut sauce: 4 tbsp peanut butter, 1 tbsp sweet soy, 1 tsp chilli paste, coconut milk, lime juice
method: Marinate tofu cubes for 15 min; thread onto soaked skewers.
Grill or pan-fry on high heat, turning, until charred at edges.
Warm peanut butter, soy sauce, chilli paste and coconut milk together; thin with lime.
Arrange skewers with cucumber and onion wedges.
Serve with peanut sauce for dipping.

name: Som Tum (Green Papaya Salad)
blurb: A bright, funky salad of shredded unripe papaya pounded with lime, chilli, palm sugar and peanuts â€” Thailand's most refreshing dish.
tip: The mortar is essential â€” bruising rather than cutting releases the papaya juices and lets the dressing penetrate.
ingredients: 2 cups green papaya, peeled and shredded
method: Pound garlic and chillies to a rough paste in a mortar.
Add palm sugar and pound briefly to dissolve.
Add long beans and tomatoes; bruise lightly with the pestle.
Add shredded papaya; toss and bruise with the pestle and spoon together.
Add lime juice, soy sauce, peanuts; toss and adjust for balance.

name: Hobak Juk (Pumpkin Porridge)
blurb: Velvety, naturally sweet Korean pumpkin porridge studded with chewy rice balls â€” a warming bowl for cold mornings.
tip: Kabocha gives the most naturally sweet and colourful juk â€” butternut works but needs a little extra sugar.
method: Boil squash in water until completely soft; blend until smooth with cooking liquid.
Return to pan over medium heat.
Mix glutinous rice flour with a little water to form a dough; roll into small balls.
Drop rice balls into simmering porridge; cook until they float.
Add sugar, salt and cinnamon; stir and serve warm.

name: Miyeokguk (Seaweed Soup)
blurb: A clean, mineral-rich broth of rehydrated sea mustard with sesame oil â€” traditionally eaten on birthdays for its restorative properties.
tip: Sauteing the seaweed in sesame oil before adding liquid gives the soup a deeper, nuttier character.
ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
method: Soak miyeok in cold water 30 min; drain, squeeze and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Heat sesame oil in a pot; saute garlic and seaweed briefly until fragrant.
Add stock; bring to a boil then simmer 15 min.
Season with soy sauce, salt and white pepper.
Serve in bowls scattered with sesame seeds.

name: Gyeran Toast (Korean Egg Toast)
blurb: A Seoul street classic â€” egg-dipped toast griddled in butter with shredded cabbage inside, finished with ketchup and a pinch of sugar.
tip: The pinch of sugar scattered over the finished toast is the street-stall touch that makes it distinctively Korean.
ingredients: Ketchup and yellow mustard to serve
method: Beat eggs with cabbage, spring onion and a pinch of salt.
Melt butter in a pan; pour egg mixture roughly the shape of the bread.
Before it fully sets, place bread on top, press, then flip so bread is underneath.
Cook until bread is golden; flip once more so egg is on top.
Transfer to plate; drizzle ketchup, a pinch of sugar and mustard.

name: Doenjang Guk with Tofu
blurb: A simple Korean soybean paste soup with soft tofu and zucchini â€” savoury, subtle and surprisingly restorative.
tip: Dissolve the doenjang gradually and taste as you go â€” different brands vary significantly in saltiness.
method: Bring stock to a simmer; dissolve doenjang into the liquid by pressing through a spoon.
Add garlic and zucchini; cook 5 min until tender.
Add tofu; simmer gently 3 min without stirring vigorously.
Taste and adjust salt if needed.
Ladle into bowls; top with spring onion and a drop of sesame oil.

name: Jangjuk (Soy Sauce Congee)
blurb: Silky Korean rice porridge seasoned with soy sauce and sesame oil â€” the most comforting answer to a cold morning.
tip: Covering the porridge for the last 5 minutes traps steam and creates an extra-silky texture.
ingredients: 4 cups water or light vegetable stock
method: Simmer rice in water on medium-low heat for 20 min, stirring occasionally, until soft and creamy.
Season with soy sauce.
Ladle into bowls; drizzle with sesame oil.
Garnish with sesame seeds and spring onion.
Serve with a small dish of kimchi on the side.

name: Bibim Guksu (Spicy Cold Noodles)
blurb: Chewy thin noodles tossed in a bright gochujang dressing with cucumber and sesame â€” a Korean summer staple.
tip: Rinsing in ice-cold water not only cools the noodles but firms the texture â€” warm noodles will clump.
ingredients: Toasted sesame seeds and a boiled egg to serve
method: Cook noodles per packet; rinse in ice-cold water until completely cold; drain well.
Whisk gochujang, soy, sugar, vinegar and sesame oil into a smooth sauce.
Toss cold noodles in the sauce until well coated.
Pile into bowls; top with cucumber, carrot and sesame seeds.
Serve immediately with a halved boiled egg.

name: Tteokbokki (Spicy Rice Cakes)
blurb: Chewy cylindrical rice cakes in a glistening gochujang and soy sauce â€” the most popular street-food comfort in Korea.
tip: The sauce should reduce and cling â€” add a splash of water only if it sticks to the pan rather than the rice cakes.
ingredients: Boiled eggs and sesame seeds to serve
method: Soak rice cakes in cold water 20 min if refrigerated.
Bring stock to a simmer; add gochujang, gochugaru, soy and sugar; stir to dissolve.
Add rice cakes; cook on medium heat 8-10 min, stirring, until sauce thickens and coats.
Add spring onions and cook 2 min more.
Serve topped with boiled eggs and sesame seeds.

name: Kongnamul Guk (Bean Sprout Soup)
blurb: A clean, restorative Korean broth of crunchy bean sprouts with garlic and sesame â€” deceptively simple, deeply flavourful.
tip: Never peek while the sprouts come to a boil â€” lifting the lid causes a bitter, grassy smell.
method: Place sprouts in a pot with water; cover and bring to a boil without lifting the lid.
Once boiling, add garlic and soy sauce; simmer 10 min.
Season with salt and gochugaru.
Turn off heat; stir in sesame oil.
Serve garnished with spring onion.

name: Dubu Jorim (Braised Tofu)
blurb: Crispy pan-fried tofu braised in a spicy, sticky gochujang and garlic sauce â€” one of Korea's most beloved everyday dishes.
tip: Patting the tofu completely dry before frying is essential â€” moisture is the enemy of a crispy crust.
ingredients: Spring onion and sesame seeds to garnish
method: Press tofu dry; pan-fry in oil until golden on both sides; set aside.
Mix gochujang, soy, sugar, garlic and water into a sauce.
Add sauce to the pan; bring to a simmer.
Return tofu; spoon sauce over and cook 5 min until sauce reduces and glazes.
Garnish with spring onion and sesame seeds.

name: Hotteok (Sweet Filled Pancake)
blurb: Yeasted street pancakes oozing with brown sugar, cinnamon and crushed walnuts â€” the iconic Korean winter snack.
tip: The dough will be sticky â€” resist adding more flour, as that stickiness creates the characteristic chewy texture.
ingredients: Filling: 3 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon, 2 tbsp chopped walnuts
method: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt and water to a sticky dough; prove 1 hour until doubled.
Mix filling ingredients together.
Grease hands; take a portion of dough, flatten, place 1 tbsp filling in centre, seal tightly.
Cook in oiled pan on medium; after 1 min, press flat with a spatula.
Flip; press again and cook 2 min until golden. Eat carefully â€” filling is very hot.

name: Gyeran Ppang (Egg Bread)
blurb: Soft, pillowy corn bread buns baked with a whole egg inside â€” a popular Korean street snack that is mildly sweet and savoury.
tip: Crack eggs from a low height so the yolk stays intact and centred â€” it looks beautiful when sliced open.
ingredients: 1 egg plus 2 extra eggs (one per bread)
Corn or grated cheese for topping
method: Mix flour, baking powder, sugar and salt; whisk in egg, milk and butter to a smooth batter.
Grease a muffin tin; fill each cavity halfway with batter.
Crack one egg carefully into each cavity on top of the batter.
Bake at 190Â°C for 15-18 min until egg is set and bread is golden.
Scatter toppings before baking for extra flavour.

name: Jeon (Korean Vegetable Pancake)
blurb: Crispy-edged savoury pancakes stuffed with zucchini, spring onion or kimchi â€” paired with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce.
tip: Using ice-cold water creates a lighter, crisper result â€” the temperature keeps gluten formation minimal.
ingredients: 1 zucchini, grated or 2 spring onions, sliced
Dipping sauce: 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sesame oil, pinch chilli flakes
method: Mix flour, egg, cold water and salt to a loose batter.
Stir in grated or sliced vegetables.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a flat pan over medium-high heat.
Pour a ladleful of batter and spread; cook 3 min until edges crisp and set.
Flip and cook 2 min more; serve with dipping sauce.

name: Bungeoppang (Red Bean Pastry)
blurb: Fish-shaped waffle cakes filled with sweet red bean paste â€” a nostalgic Korean winter street snack.
tip: Ready-made red bean paste from an Asian grocery gives consistent results every time.
method: Whisk flour, baking powder and sugar; beat in egg, milk and butter to a smooth batter.
Heat a sandwich maker or bungeoppang mould and brush with oil.
Pour batter into one side to half-fill; add 2 tbsp red bean paste.
Cover with more batter; close the mould and cook 3 min each side.
Unmould and eat warm â€” the filling will be very hot.

name: Yakgwa (Honey Sesame Cookie)
blurb: Delicately fried Korean honey cookies perfumed with ginger and sesame, soaked in a fragrant sugar syrup.
tip: Frying at very low temperature is essential â€” high heat burns the outside while the inside stays raw.
ingredients: Pinch of salt and ginger powder
Syrup: 1/2 cup honey, 1/4 cup water, 1 tsp ginger juice
Sesame seeds and pine nuts to garnish
method: Mix flour with sesame oil, honey, rice wine, salt and ginger until crumbly; press into a dough.
Roll to 1cm thick; stamp into round or square shapes.
Fry in oil at 150Â°C (very low) for 12-15 min until golden throughout.
Drain; dip immediately into warm honey syrup for 30 min.
Drain again; press sesame seeds and pine nuts on top.

name: Zaru Soba (Cold Buckwheat Noodles)
blurb: Chilled buckwheat noodles served on a bamboo tray with a cold dashi dipping broth â€” clean, elegant and deeply refreshing.
tip: Rinse the soba under cold water with vigour â€” the friction removes excess starch and gives each strand a clean, firm bite.
ingredients: Wasabi and grated ginger to serve
method: Cook soba per packet; drain and rinse immediately under cold running water until completely chilled.
Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar; simmer 2 min; cool completely.
Arrange soba on a tray or plate; scatter nori on top.
Pour dipping broth into a small bowl.
Dip noodles in broth with spring onion, wasabi and ginger; eat immediately.

name: Tofu Katsu Curry
blurb: Panko-crusted tofu cutlets on steamed rice with a thick, subtly spiced Japanese curry sauce â€” comfort food at its most satisfying.
tip: Refrigerating the breaded tofu for 10 minutes before frying helps the panko adhere and prevents it falling off in the oil.
ingredients: For curry sauce: 1 onion, 1 carrot, 2 potatoes, 2 tbsp curry roux (S&B or similar)
method: Dredge tofu in flour, dip in egg, coat in panko; refrigerate 10 min.
Simmer onion, carrot and potato in stock until tender; add curry roux and stir until smooth.
Fry breaded tofu in 170Â°C oil until golden and crisp; drain.
Serve rice in a bowl, ladle curry alongside.
Place tofu katsu on top; garnish with spring onion and pickled ginger.

name: Kinoko Gohan (Mushroom Rice)
blurb: Fragrant Japanese rice cooked with a medley of mushrooms, soy and sake â€” a deeply umami one-pot that celebrates the earthy forest floor.
tip: Removing the kombu before the rice finishes cooking prevents it from becoming slimy â€” 15 minutes of infusing is enough.
ingredients: Spring onion and toasted sesame to garnish
method: Soak rice in water 30 min; drain.
Slice mushrooms; sautÃ© in a little oil until golden and fragrant.
Combine rice, sauteed mushrooms, soy, sake, mirin, kombu and water in a rice cooker or pot.
Cook as normal rice; remove kombu before serving.
Fluff with a spoon; garnish with spring onion and sesame.

name: Ochazuke (Rice with Green Tea and Nori)
blurb: Leftover rice revived with hot green tea, pickled plum and nori â€” Japan's most contemplative and comforting light meal.
tip: Hojicha (roasted green tea) gives a nuttier, smoother flavour than sencha â€” try both and see which you prefer.
ingredients: 1 cup hot green tea (sencha or hojicha)
method: Place rice in a bowl; arrange nori strips, umeboshi and spring onion on top.
Pour hot green tea over the rice.
Add soy sauce; stir gently.
Add a small dot of wasabi if using.
Eat immediately before the nori softens too much.

name: Yudofu (Simmered Tofu in Kombu Broth)
blurb: Silken tofu gently heated in a clean kombu broth, eaten dipped in ponzu and grated ginger â€” the most meditative dish in Japanese cuisine.
tip: Never let the broth boil â€” simmering silently is the point; boiling makes silken tofu fall apart and turns the broth bitter.
method: Soak kombu in water for 30 min; bring to a very gentle simmer.
Add tofu pieces; heat slowly until warmed through â€” do not boil.
Mix ponzu, grated ginger, daikon and spring onion for dipping sauce.
Serve tofu directly from the pot; dip each piece into the sauce.
Sip the warm kombu broth between bites.

name: Miso Ramen (Vegetarian)
blurb: Rich, cloudy miso broth with springy noodles, corn, bamboo shoots and a drizzle of chilli oil â€” warming from first sip to last.
tip: Add miso off the heat or at a very gentle simmer â€” boiling destroys its probiotic cultures and dulls the flavour.
ingredients: Toppings: corn, bamboo shoots, soft-boiled egg, nori, spring onion, chilli oil
method: Simmer stock with garlic and ginger 5 min; whisk in miso and soy sauce â€” do not boil after adding miso.
Stir in sesame oil.
Cook noodles per packet; drain and divide into bowls.
Pour hot miso broth over noodles.
Arrange toppings artfully and drizzle chilli oil; serve immediately.

name: Japanese Vegetable Curry
blurb: A thick, gentle curry of root vegetables in a rich, subtly spiced sauce served over steamed rice â€” Japan's most popular home-cooked dish.
tip: The curry roux needs 5 full minutes of simmering after melting to thicken properly and lose any raw flour taste.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Japanese curry roux (S&B Golden Curry)
method: Saute onion in oil until softened; add carrots and potatoes and fry 3 min.
Add water or stock; bring to a boil and simmer 15 min until vegetables are nearly tender.
Add courgette; cook 5 min more.
Break in curry roux blocks; stir until completely melted and sauce thickens.
Season with soy sauce and serve over rice with pickle on the side.

name: Vegetarian Sukiyaki
blurb: A Japanese hot-pot of vegetables, tofu and glass noodles simmered in a sweet soy broth, dipped in raw egg â€” indulgent and communal.
tip: Keep the heat at a gentle simmer throughout â€” rapid boiling makes the tofu rubbery and breaks down the delicate vegetables.
method: Mix soy, mirin, sake and sugar into a warishita (sukiyaki sauce).
Heat a wide shallow pan; pour in half the sauce and bring to a simmer.
Add tofu, leek, cabbage and mushrooms; cook until tender, adding more sauce as needed.
Add glass noodles; simmer until translucent.
Beat eggs lightly in small bowls; dip each bite before eating (or skip the egg for vegan).

name: Yakimeshi (Japanese Fried Rice)
blurb: Wok-fried Japanese rice with egg, spring onion and soy â€” simpler than Chinese fried rice, subtler in flavour and deeply habit-forming.
tip: Day-old rice from the fridge is drier and fries better â€” fresh rice turns mushy and clumps.
ingredients: 2 cups cooked short-grain rice (day-old is best)
method: Heat wok on high; add oil and scramble eggs until just set; break into pieces.
Add cold rice; press and stir-fry vigorously, breaking up any clumps.
Add soy and oyster sauce; toss until every grain is coated and starting to char slightly.
Add spring onion and white pepper; toss 30 seconds more.
Drizzle sesame oil; serve immediately with pickled ginger.

name: Edamame with Sea Salt
blurb: Boiled young soybeans in the pod, scattered with flaky sea salt â€” the purest, most effortless Japanese snack.
tip: Salting both the cooking water and the finished edamame in two stages gives a more flavourful result than just one.
method: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil; add salt generously.
Add frozen edamame; cook 4-5 min until bright green and tender.
Drain; toss immediately with a pinch of flaky salt.
Serve in a bowl with a small dish for the empty pods.
Squeeze lemon over if desired.

name: Yakitori Tofu Skewers
blurb: Tender tofu cubes glazed with a sweet soy tare and grilled until caramelised at the edges â€” the vegetarian answer to Japan's most beloved skewer.
tip: Press the tofu for at least 20 minutes before skewering â€” drier tofu holds together better and caramelises more evenly.
ingredients: Toasted sesame seeds and shichimi to garnish
method: Simmer soy, mirin, sake and sugar in a small pan until slightly thickened; cool.
Thread tofu and spring onion alternately onto skewers.
Grill or pan-fry on medium-high heat, turning every 2 min.
Brush tare glaze over skewers during last 2 min of cooking.
Scatter sesame seeds and shichimi; serve immediately.

name: Jianbing (Vegetable Savoury Crepe)
blurb: A crispy, layered Beijing street crepe with egg, hoisin, crispy wonton and spring onion â€” China's most beloved breakfast on the go.
tip: The batter should be almost as thin as water â€” a thick crepe loses the characteristic papery crispness.
ingredients: 1/2 cup mung bean flour (or plain flour)
method: Mix flour and water to a thin smooth batter.
Heat a non-stick pan; pour a thin layer of batter and swirl to coat.
Crack an egg on top; spread with the back of a spoon.
Sprinkle spring onion and bean sprouts; cook until egg sets.
Spread hoisin and chilli sauce, add coriander and crispy wonton; fold and serve.

name: Steamed Vegetable Baozi (Buns)
blurb: Pillowy steamed yeast buns filled with seasoned cabbage, tofu and mushroom â€” the most comforting Chinese breakfast.
tip: Squeezing excess water from the cabbage filling before stuffing prevents soggy, leaking buns.
ingredients: Filling: 1 cup napa cabbage, 100g tofu, 50g shiitake mushrooms
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, ginger, spring onion
method: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and water to a smooth dough; prove 1 hour until doubled.
Finely chop filling ingredients; mix with soy, sesame oil, ginger and salt; squeeze out excess liquid.
Divide dough into 8; roll each into a circle; place 1 tbsp filling in centre.
Gather and pleat edges to seal; prove 15 min more.
Steam over high heat for 15 min; rest 2 min before lifting lid.

name: Red Bean Porridge
blurb: A gentle, lightly sweetened porridge of soft red beans and glutinous rice â€” a Chinese breakfast with quietly nourishing depth.
tip: Soaking the beans overnight halves the cooking time and produces a creamier, more evenly cooked porridge.
ingredients: 1/2 cup red adzuki beans, soaked overnight
Dried tangerine peel or a pandan leaf (optional)
method: Drain soaked beans; simmer in fresh water with tangerine peel or pandan for 45 min until very soft.
Add rinsed glutinous rice; cook 20 min more, stirring occasionally, until porridge is thick.
Add sugar and salt; stir to dissolve.
Remove peel or pandan.
Serve warm; leftovers thicken overnight â€” thin with a little water when reheating.

name: Dan Dan Noodles (Vegetarian)
blurb: Chewy noodles in a fiery, numbing sauce of sesame, chilli oil and Sichuan pepper â€” one of China's most electrically flavoured dishes.
tip: Using the hot noodle cooking water to loosen the sauce emulsifies it beautifully and helps it cling to every strand.
ingredients: 3 tbsp tahini or Chinese sesame paste
Spring onion and crushed peanuts to garnish
method: Cook noodles per packet; drain, reserving 3 tbsp cooking water.
Whisk tahini, chilli oil, soy, vinegar, Sichuan pepper, sugar and garlic; loosen with cooking water.
Toss hot noodles in the sauce immediately.
Transfer to bowls; top with spring onion and peanuts.
Add extra chilli oil at the table.

name: Buddha's Delight (Lo Han Jai)
blurb: A rich, glistening Buddhist temple stew of tofu, glass noodles, cloud ear mushrooms and lotus root â€” eaten on the first day of Lunar New Year for good fortune.
tip: This dish improves overnight as the flavours meld â€” make it the evening before for the best result.
method: Soak glass noodles and cloud ear mushrooms separately for 30 min; drain.
Fry tofu until golden; set aside.
Heat oil; stir-fry carrot, lotus root and cabbage 3 min.
Add mushrooms, tofu, soy, oyster sauce and sugar; toss well.
Add noodles and 1/2 cup water; simmer 8 min until glossy and sauce has absorbed; finish with sesame oil.

name: Winter Melon and Tofu Soup
blurb: A delicate, clear Chinese soup of winter melon and silken tofu in a light ginger broth â€” cooling, restorative and effortlessly elegant.
tip: Do not stir the soup after adding tofu â€” silken tofu breaks apart easily and the clear broth is part of the beauty.
ingredients: 400g winter melon, peeled, seeded and cubed
Salt and white pepper to taste
Spring onion and coriander to garnish
method: Bring stock to a simmer with ginger slices.
Add winter melon; simmer 15 min until just translucent.
Gently slide in tofu; simmer 3 min.
Season with soy sauce, salt and white pepper.
Ladle into bowls; drizzle sesame oil and scatter spring onion and coriander.

name: Mushroom and Tofu Clay Pot
blurb: A warming, fragrant clay pot of shiitake mushrooms and braised tofu in a dark, glossy soy and oyster sauce â€” the soul of Chinese home cooking.
tip: A genuine clay pot retains heat beautifully but any heavy-bottomed pan works â€” the key is the slow simmer.
ingredients: 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
method: Fry tofu cubes in hot oil until golden; drain.
Saute garlic until fragrant; add mushrooms and carrot; fry 3 min.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine and sugar; stir.
Add tofu and 1/2 cup water; simmer 10 min until sauce thickens.
Add spring onion; drizzle sesame oil and season with white pepper; serve in the clay pot.

name: Tofu Pudding (Douhua)
blurb: Silky-soft tofu pudding served warm with a fragrant ginger sugar syrup â€” Shanghai's most gentle and beloved street snack.
tip: Scoop douhua with a flat-edged spoon in a single sweeping motion to lift whole sheets without breaking them.
ingredients: 400g fresh silken tofu (or douhua from Asian grocery)
For syrup: 3 tbsp sugar, 1 cup water, 2 cm ginger, smashed
Optional toppings: azuki beans, taro balls, peanuts
method: Simmer sugar, water and ginger until sugar dissolves; remove ginger.
Gently scoop douhua into bowls with a wide spoon â€” do not stir or it breaks.
Pour warm ginger syrup over.
Add toppings if using.
Serve immediately while warm.

name: Sesame Tang Yuan (Rice Balls)
blurb: Glutinous rice balls filled with a molten black sesame paste centre, served in a sweet ginger broth â€” the centrepiece of the Lantern Festival.
tip: Chilling the sesame filling firms it so it can be wrapped cleanly â€” warm filling is too soft to handle.
ingredients: Filling: 4 tbsp black sesame powder, 3 tbsp icing sugar, 3 tbsp butter or lard
For broth: 3 cups water, 3 tbsp sugar, 3 slices ginger
method: Mix sesame powder, icing sugar and butter until a stiff paste; refrigerate 15 min; roll into small balls.
Mix rice flour and water to a smooth, pliable dough.
Flatten a dough piece, place a sesame ball inside; seal and roll into a ball.
Simmer ginger broth; drop tang yuan in; cook until they float plus 2 min more.
Serve in ginger broth while hot.

name: Vegetable Spring Rolls
blurb: Thin, shatteringly crispy fried rolls stuffed with glass noodles, cabbage and carrot â€” the Chinese snack that travels the world.
tip: Cooling the filling completely before wrapping is essential â€” hot filling creates steam that makes the wrapper soggy.
method: Stir-fry cabbage, carrot and garlic until softened; add noodles, soy and sesame oil; cool completely.
Place a spring roll wrapper on a flat surface at 45 degrees.
Spoon filling in a line across the lower third; fold bottom corner over filling.
Fold sides in and roll tightly to the top; seal with a paste of flour and water.
Deep fry at 180Â°C until golden and crisp, about 3-4 min; drain and serve.

name: Peanut Sesame Noodles
blurb: Cold wheat noodles tossed in a rich, nutty peanut and sesame sauce with cucumber and chilli â€” a satisfying Chinese snack any time of day.
tip: A splash of warm water while whisking is the trick that transforms chunky peanut butter into a silky, pourable sauce.
ingredients: Spring onion and sesame seeds to garnish
method: Cook noodles per packet; drain and rinse under cold water; cool completely.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, vinegar, sugar and chilli with a splash of warm water until smooth.
Toss cold noodles in the sauce.
Top with cucumber, spring onion and sesame seeds.
Serve cold or at room temperature.

name: Menemen (Turkish Scrambled Eggs with Peppers)
blurb: A Turkish classic of eggs gently scrambled into a simmering sauce of tomatoes, peppers and spices — Istanbul in a pan.
tip: The key to menemen is patience — stir slowly and remove from heat while still slightly underdone; carryover heat finishes it perfectly.
method: Heat olive oil; saute onion until soft, add peppers and cook 5 min.
Add tomatoes and spices; simmer 8 min until sauce thickens.
Beat eggs lightly and pour over the tomato mixture.
Stir gently and slowly until eggs are softly set — do not over-scramble.
Garnish with parsley; serve straight from the pan with crusty bread.

name: Borek with Spinach and Feta
blurb: Layers of flaky filo pastry encasing a salty, herbed spinach and feta filling — Turkey's most beloved savoury pastry, straight from the oven.
tip: Work with filo quickly and keep unused sheets covered with a damp cloth — it dries and tears within minutes of exposure.
ingredients: 3 tbsp olive oil and 2 tbsp butter, melted together
method: Mix spinach with feta, one egg, onion, nutmeg and seasoning.
Brush a baking dish with butter; lay two sheets of filo, brushing each with butter mixture.
Spread half the filling; add two more buttered filo sheets; repeat layers.
Finish with two filo sheets, buttered on top; score into diamonds.
Beat remaining egg and brush over; scatter sesame seeds; bake at 190°C for 30-35 min until golden.

name: Kaymak Toast with Honey and Walnuts
blurb: Thick, clotted-cream-style kaymak spread on toasted bread and drizzled with dark floral honey and crushed walnuts — a Levantine luxury breakfast.
tip: Source the best-quality honey you can find — this simple dish lives and dies by the quality of two ingredients.
ingredients: 4 slices thick sourdough or simit bread, toasted
3 tbsp dark honey (preferably pine or thyme honey)
method: Toast bread until golden.
Spread kaymak generously over each slice.
Drizzle honey liberally over the kaymak.
Scatter crushed walnuts and dust with cinnamon.
Serve immediately with fresh fruit and tea.

name: Freekeh Salad with Fresh Herbs
blurb: Nutty, smoky freekeh grain tossed with a confetti of fresh parsley, mint, tomato and a bright lemon dressing — the Levantine grain salad to know.
tip: Cool the freekeh completely before adding the herbs — warm grain wilts them and dulls their bright colour.
method: Rinse freekeh; simmer in 2 cups water for 20 min until tender; drain and cool.
Combine parsley, mint, tomato, cucumber and spring onion in a large bowl.
Add cooled freekeh; toss gently.
Dress with olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper; toss again.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds and serve at room temperature.

name: Falafel and Hummus Wrap
blurb: Crispy, herb-packed falafel in a warm flatbread with creamy hummus, fresh vegetables and tangy tahini — the street-food wrap that feeds the world.
tip: The tahini sauce is the soul of the wrap — thin it with water and lemon until it pours like double cream.
ingredients: 2 tbsp tahini sauce (tahini, lemon, water, garlic)
method: Fry or bake falafel until deeply golden and crispy.
Warm flatbreads directly on a gas flame or dry pan for 30 seconds.
Spread hummus generously on each flatbread.
Add cucumber, tomato, onion and herbs.
Place falafel on top; drizzle tahini sauce; roll tightly and serve.

name: Lentil Soup (Shorbat Adas)
blurb: A velvety, golden soup of red lentils perfumed with cumin and finished with a sizzle of lemon and olive oil — the staple of Levantine homes.
tip: A squeeze of lemon just before serving is not optional — it brightens the whole soup and balances the earthiness of the lentils.
ingredients: Toasted bread croutons and fresh parsley to garnish
method: Saute onion in olive oil until golden; add garlic and cumin, fry 1 min.
Add lentils, turmeric and stock; bring to a boil and simmer 20 min until lentils dissolve.
Blend until completely smooth; return to pan.
Adjust consistency and seasoning; add lemon juice.
Ladle into bowls; drizzle olive oil; garnish with parsley and croutons.

name: Koshari (Rice, Lentils and Crispy Onions)
blurb: Egypt's beloved street food — a triumphant pile of rice, lentils, pasta and crispy fried onions drenched in spiced tomato sauce.
tip: The crispy onions are what make koshari extraordinary — fry them low and slow until caramel-dark, not just golden.
ingredients: For tomato sauce: 2 cups tomato puree, 4 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, chilli
method: Cook lentils 20 min until just tender; cook rice separately; cook pasta separately.
Fry onion rings in oil until deeply golden and crisp; drain on paper.
Saute garlic for tomato sauce; add tomato puree, spices and a splash of vinegar; simmer 10 min.
Layer rice, then lentils, then pasta in a serving bowl.
Top with crispy onions and pour tomato sauce over; serve.

name: Vegetarian Moussaka
blurb: Layers of roasted aubergine, spiced lentils and a thick bechamel crust — the Greek and Levantine classic in its most satisfying vegetarian form.
tip: Resting the moussaka before cutting is essential — it firms up and holds its layers when sliced.
ingredients: 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp allspice, 1 tsp cumin
For bechamel: 3 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp flour, 2 cups milk, nutmeg, 1 egg yolk
method: Brush aubergine slices with oil; roast at 200°C for 20 min until golden.
Saute onion and garlic; add tomatoes and spices; stir in cooked lentils and simmer 10 min.
Make bechamel: melt butter, stir in flour, whisk in hot milk until thick; season with nutmeg; stir in egg yolk.
Layer in a baking dish: lentil mixture, aubergine slices, bechamel on top.
Bake at 180°C for 30 min until bechamel is golden and set; rest 10 min before cutting.

name: Stuffed Peppers (Dolma)
blurb: Vibrant bell peppers filled with herbed rice, pine nuts and currants, baked until tender — a jewel of the Levantine table.
tip: Parboiling the rice just halfway before stuffing ensures it finishes cooking perfectly inside the pepper without being crunchy.
ingredients: 2 tbsp flat-leaf parsley and mint, chopped
method: Fry onion in olive oil until soft; add pine nuts and fry until golden.
Mix with parboiled rice, currants, herbs and spices; season well.
Slice tops off peppers; remove seeds; fill each one firmly with rice mixture.
Place in a baking dish; pour tomato juice around; drizzle olive oil.
Cover with foil; bake at 180°C for 35 min; uncover last 5 min to colour tops.

name: Couscous with Seven Vegetables
blurb: A Moroccan-inspired mound of steamed couscous crowned with sweet, saffron-spiced vegetables — a feast dish in spirit and in practice.
tip: A generous knob of butter stirred into the couscous as it steams gives it the fluffiness that distinguishes a great dish from a flat one.
method: Saute onion in oil; add spices and saffron water; cook 1 min.
Add carrots, pumpkin and 2 cups water; simmer 10 min.
Add courgettes and chickpeas; simmer 8 min more.
Pour boiling stock over couscous with butter and salt; cover and rest 5 min; fluff with a fork.
Mound couscous in a serving dish; crown with vegetables and broth.

name: Kibbeh Nayeh (Bulgur and Herb Croquette)
blurb: Crispy bulgur wheat croquettes packed with herbs and warming spices — the vegetarian version of one of the Levant's oldest dishes.
tip: Fine bulgur is essential — coarse bulgur will not bind properly and the croquettes will fall apart in the pan.
ingredients: 1 cup fine bulgur wheat, soaked and drained
method: Mix soaked, drained bulgur with grated onion, spices, salt and parsley until it holds together.
Taste the raw mix — adjust seasoning now.
Shape into small oval patties; press a pine nut into the centre of each.
Shallow-fry in hot oil 3 min each side until golden crust forms.
Drain; serve with yoghurt, mint and a squeeze of lemon.

name: Hoppers (Appa) with Coconut Sambol
blurb: Bowl-shaped fermented rice crepes with crispy lacey edges and a soft centre, served with a fiery, tangy coconut sambol.
tip: The fermentation is the soul of a good hopper — a 6-hour batter produces a mildly sour, airy crepe with perfect edge crispiness.
ingredients: For sambol: 1 cup fresh coconut grated, 2 red chillies, 1/2 onion, lime juice, salt
method: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, water, yeast and sugar; ferment 6-8 hrs until bubbly and slightly sour.
Prepare sambol: blend coconut with chilli and onion coarsely; add lime juice and salt; toss.
Heat a hopper pan (or small wok); grease lightly; pour a ladle of batter and swirl to coat sides.
Cover and cook 2-3 min until edges are golden and crisp; centre should remain soft.
Serve hoppers immediately with coconut sambol.

name: String Hoppers (Idiyappam) with Coconut Gravy
blurb: Steamed rice flour noodle nests served with a silky, mildly spiced coconut milk gravy — the lighter, more delicate cousin of the hopper.
tip: Work the dough while warm — as it cools it becomes stiff and will not press through the mould smoothly.
ingredients: For coconut gravy: 1 cup thin coconut milk, 1/2 cup thick coconut milk, 1 onion, 1 green chilli, curry leaves, mustard seeds
method: Pour boiling water over rice flour with salt; mix to a pliable dough.
Press dough through a string hopper press onto steaming discs; steam 5-8 min until cooked.
Saute onion, chilli and curry leaves; add thin coconut milk and simmer 5 min.
Stir in thick coconut milk; heat gently without boiling; season.
Serve string hopper nests with warm coconut gravy poured over.

name: Kiribath (Milk Rice)
blurb: Thick, creamy rice cooked in coconut milk until each grain is enveloped in richness — a Sri Lankan celebration dish eaten at every auspicious occasion.
tip: Kiribath thickens as it cools, so remove from heat while it looks slightly looser than desired — it will set perfectly in the tray.
ingredients: Coconut sambol or jaggery to serve
method: Bring water and rice to a boil; cook 10 min until water absorbs.
Add coconut milk and salt; stir and cook on very low heat 15 min, stirring occasionally.
Rice should be thick and creamy with no liquid pooling.
Pour into a greased tray and press flat; cool slightly.
Cut into diamond shapes; serve with sambol for savoury or jaggery for sweet.

name: Roti with Coconut Sambol
blurb: Soft, griddle-cooked coconut flatbreads alongside a punchy, fresh coconut and chilli relish — a Sri Lankan morning ritual.
tip: Desiccated coconut in the dough gives the roti a characteristic texture and subtle sweetness distinct from plain flatbread.
ingredients: Sambol: 1 cup fresh grated coconut, 3 dried red chillies, 1/2 onion, lime, salt
method: Mix flour, coconut, salt and oil; add water gradually to form a soft, pliable dough.
Rest 10 min; divide and roll each portion into a thin circle.
Cook on a dry hot griddle 2 min each side until lightly charred.
For sambol: blend chillies and onion to a paste; mix into coconut with salt and lime juice.
Serve warm roti with sambol alongside.

name: Pittu with Coconut Milk
blurb: A steamed cylinder of rice flour and coconut that crumbles into the mouth — served with warm coconut milk and a drizzle of sweetened condensed milk for a truly Sri Lankan morning.
tip: The mixture should feel like damp sand — too wet and it becomes gummy; too dry and it will not steam into a cohesive cylinder.
ingredients: 1 cup warm coconut milk to serve
Banana leaf strips or bamboo pittu mould
method: Mix rice flour, coconut and salt; add water tablespoon by tablespoon until the mixture holds when squeezed but crumbles when released.
Fill a bamboo pittu steamer in alternating layers of mixture and coconut.
Steam over boiling water for 10-12 min.
Turn out onto a plate; the cylinder should hold its shape.
Serve with warm coconut milk poured over and condensed milk drizzled on top.

name: Sri Lankan Rice and Curry Plate
blurb: A full Sri Lankan lunch plate — mounds of rice surrounded by three or four curries, a sambola and a pickle — a complete meal in one glorious spread.
tip: The genius of a Sri Lankan rice and curry plate is balance — make sure at least one component is cooling (coconut) to offset the heat.
method: Steam rice; make dal curry by simmering red lentils with coconut milk, turmeric and tempered mustard seeds.
Prepare a simple potato curry with curry powder, coconut milk and curry leaves.
Arrange rice on a banana leaf or plate; surround with small portions of each curry.
Place sambol and pickle on the side.
Serve with papadoms and encourage eating with the right hand in the traditional style.

name: Dhal Curry with Rice (Sri Lankan)
blurb: Sri Lanka's most comforting everyday dish — silky red lentils simmered with coconut milk, green chilli and curry leaves.
tip: Sri Lankan dal is meant to be softer and creamier than Indian dal — do not stop cooking at the al dente stage.
method: Cook lentils with water, turmeric and green chilli until soft and breaking down.
Add coconut milk; stir and simmer 5 min; season with salt.
Heat oil; splutter mustard seeds and cumin; add onion and curry leaves; fry until golden.
Pour tempering over dal; stir gently.
Serve over steamed rice.

name: Gotukola Sambol with Rice
blurb: Steamed rice served with a fresh, raw coconut and gotukola (pennywort) salad — a uniquely Sri Lankan herb-forward accompaniment.
tip: Gotukola sambol is best eaten fresh and raw — do not dress it ahead of time as the lime wilts the leaves quickly.
ingredients: 2 cups gotukola (pennywort) or watercress, finely chopped
method: Cook rice until fluffy.
Combine gotukola with coconut, onion and green chilli.
Add lime juice and salt; toss and taste — it should be sharp, fresh and slightly spicy.
Serve a generous mound of sambol alongside hot rice.
Add a pappadom for crunch.

name: Tempered Lentil Rice
blurb: Rice cooked with lentils and tempered with mustard, curry leaves and crispy onion — a Sri Lankan one-pot that is more than the sum of its parts.
tip: The tempering should be smoking hot when it hits the rice — the sizzle and fragrance is the signature of this dish.
method: Rinse rice and lentils together; bring to a boil in salted water with turmeric.
Simmer 20 min until both are cooked and water absorbed.
Heat coconut oil until very hot; splutter mustard seeds, cumin and dried chillies.
Add onion and curry leaves; fry until onion is deeply golden and crisp.
Pour sizzling tempering over rice; fold gently and serve.

name: Jackfruit Curry with Rice
blurb: Young jackfruit simmered in a coconut milk and Sri Lankan spice gravy until tender and flavourful — a meaty, satisfying curry.
tip: Canned young green jackfruit works perfectly here — rinse thoroughly to remove the brine before adding to the curry.
method: If using fresh jackfruit, boil in salted water 20 min until tender; drain.
Saute onion, garlic and curry leaves in oil until golden.
Add curry powder, turmeric and lemongrass; fry 1 min.
Add jackfruit and coconut milk; simmer 20 min until gravy thickens.
Serve over rice.

name: Jackfruit Curry (Polos)
blurb: A bold, dark Sri Lankan curry of young jackfruit that has absorbed a complex paste of roasted spices and tamarind — the island's most celebrated vegetarian curry.
tip: Using roasted (not raw) Sri Lankan curry powder is what gives polos its characteristic dark, complex flavour.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Sri Lankan roasted curry powder
method: Boil jackfruit until tender; drain and roughly pull apart into chunks.
Saute onion with pandan and lemongrass until golden.
Add roasted curry powder, chilli and turmeric; fry 2 min.
Add jackfruit, tamarind, salt and coconut milk; simmer 20 min until gravy is deep and rich.
Adjust salt; remove lemongrass; serve with roti or rice.

name: Wambatu Moju (Eggplant Pickle Curry)
blurb: Fried aubergine in a sweet, tangy and hot vinegar-based pickle sauce — one of the most distinctive Sri Lankan side dishes.
tip: Salting and rinsing the aubergine before frying draws out moisture and gives a crisper, less oil-absorbent result.
ingredients: 2 large aubergines, cubed and salted 15 min
method: Rinse and dry salted aubergine; deep-fry in batches until golden; drain.
Fry onion rings until crisp; drain.
In a little oil, fry mustard seeds; add vinegar, sugar, turmeric and pepper; bring to a simmer.
Add fried aubergine, onion and green chillies; toss to coat.
Cool before serving — the pickle is better at room temperature and improves overnight.

name: Sri Lankan Potato Curry (Ala Thel Dala)
blurb: Dry-fried potatoes in a thick Sri Lankan spice paste with coconut milk — a rustic, intensely flavoured everyday curry.
tip: Cooking uncovered after adding coconut milk allows the moisture to evaporate and leaves the potatoes in a clingy spice coating rather than a watery curry.
ingredients: Salt and lime juice to finish
method: Parboil potatoes 8 min until just starting to soften; drain.
Heat coconut oil; fry onion with curry leaves until golden.
Add curry powder, turmeric and chilli; fry 1 min.
Add potatoes; toss to coat in spices.
Add coconut milk and salt; cook uncovered until liquid reduces and potatoes are coated in a thick, dry sauce; finish with lime.

name: Ulundu Vadai (Urad Dal Fritter)
blurb: Crispy, golden doughnuts of urad dal batter spiced with cumin and green chilli — the Sri Lankan vadai, eaten with coconut sambol.
tip: Grind the dal with as little water as possible — a thick batter gives a lighter, crisper vadai; too thin and they will absorb oil and turn heavy.
method: Drain and grind urad dal with minimal water to a thick, smooth batter; it should hold its shape.
Fold in cumin, chillies, onion and curry leaves.
Wet hands; shape batter into a flat disc and make a hole in the centre.
Deep fry at 175°C until golden on both sides — about 3-4 min total.
Drain; serve hot with coconut sambol.

name: Kokis (Crispy Coconut Snack)
blurb: Intricately shaped, crispy Sri Lankan cookies made by dipping a hot iron mould into coconut batter and frying — a Sinhala New Year staple.
tip: The mould must be very hot before dipping in batter — this is what causes the characteristic crispy, lacy texture.
ingredients: Oil for deep frying (and for the kokis mould)
Kokis mould (a special iron mould with a flower or geometric pattern)
method: Whisk rice flour, coconut milk, egg and salt into a smooth, thin batter.
Heat oil in a deep pan; submerge the kokis mould in the hot oil for 1 min to heat through.
Dip the hot mould into the batter up to the rim — it should sizzle.
Immediately submerge mould back in oil; the batter will puff and release from the mould.
Fry until golden and crisp; drain; cool fully before storing.

name: Konda Kavum (Rice Flour Sweet)
blurb: Deep-fried Sri Lankan sweetmeats made from rice flour and jaggery — golden, soft within and slightly crispy outside, traditionally made for Sinhala New Year.
tip: Frying at a lower temperature is essential — kavum needs time to cook through before the outside browns.
ingredients: 1/2 cup jaggery or dark brown sugar, dissolved in 1 cup water
method: Strain dissolved jaggery; mix with coconut milk and turmeric.
Gradually add liquid to rice flour, mixing to a thick, smooth batter that is pourable.
Heat oil to 160°C; drop heaped tablespoons of batter in.
Fry slowly, spooning oil over the top, until golden and cooked through — about 5-6 min.
Drain; cool slightly; the texture should be slightly chewy inside.

name: Thala Guli (Sesame Energy Ball)
blurb: Compact, intensely nutty balls of toasted sesame and jaggery — Sri Lanka's original energy snack, made without any cooking.
tip: Roll the balls while the mixture is still warm — once cooled, it becomes too stiff and crumbles rather than binding.
ingredients: 4 tbsp jaggery or dark brown sugar
method: Dry-toast sesame seeds in a pan on low heat, stirring constantly, until golden and fragrant; cool.
Blend half the sesame to a rough powder; leave the other half whole for texture.
Warm jaggery with honey until melted; mix into sesame off the heat.
Add cardamom and salt; mix well.
While still warm, roll into small balls; cool completely to firm up.

name: Avocado Toast with Poached Egg
blurb: Creamy mashed avocado on toasted sourdough topped with a softly poached egg, lemon and chilli flakes — the modern brunch classic that earned its reputation.
tip: Do not blend the avocado — a rough mash with visible chunks has far better texture than a smooth paste.
ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil to drizzle
Microgreens or radish slices to garnish
method: Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer; add vinegar.
Mash avocado with lemon juice, salt and pepper to a rough, textured mash.
Swirl the simmering water; slide eggs in and poach 3 min until whites are just set.
Spread avocado generously on toast; top with a poached egg.
Drizzle olive oil; scatter chilli flakes and garnish; serve immediately.

name: Bircher Muesli
blurb: Rolled oats soaked overnight in apple juice with yoghurt and grated apple — a Swiss morning staple that is creamy, fresh and completely no-cook.
tip: Grating the apple just before serving (rather than the night before) prevents browning and keeps the flavour bright and fresh.
ingredients: Handful of toasted nuts to scatter
method: Mix oats with apple juice; stir, cover and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, stir in yoghurt, grated apple, honey and cinnamon.
Add a splash of milk if the consistency is too thick.
Spoon into bowls; top with berries, seeds and toasted nuts.
Serve straight from the fridge — it is meant to be eaten cold.

name: French Toast with Berries
blurb: Thick-cut bread soaked in a vanilla and cinnamon egg custard and fried until golden — the Gallic classic served with fresh berries and a maple drizzle.
tip: Use day-old brioche — it is slightly drier and absorbs the custard without becoming soggy.
ingredients: 4 slices thick brioche or challah bread
method: Whisk eggs, milk, vanilla and cinnamon until smooth.
Soak bread slices in the custard 30 seconds each side until saturated.
Melt butter in a wide pan over medium heat.
Fry soaked bread 2-3 min each side until deeply golden.
Serve with fresh berries, a drizzle of maple syrup and a dusting of icing sugar.

name: Croque Madame (Vegetarian)
blurb: A grilled gruyere and mustard sandwich covered in bechamel and crowned with a fried egg — the grande dame of French cafe sandwiches in a vegetarian guise.
tip: The bechamel should be very thick — it needs to hold its shape on top of the bread without dripping.
ingredients: 4 slices sourdough or white sandwich bread
For bechamel: 1 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp flour, 150ml milk, pinch of nutmeg
method: Make bechamel: melt butter, stir in flour 1 min, whisk in milk until smooth and thick; season with nutmeg.
Spread mustard inside sandwiches; fill with most of the cheese; press together.
Toast sandwiches in a buttered pan 2 min each side until golden.
Place on a baking tray; spread bechamel on top; scatter remaining cheese; grill 3-4 min until bubbling.
Top each sandwich with a fried egg; serve immediately.

name: Eggs Benedict Florentine
blurb: English muffins topped with wilted spinach and poached eggs under a cascade of rich, lemony hollandaise — the most luxurious vegetarian eggs Benedict.
tip: Hollandaise splits when too hot — keep the water at a gentle simmer and remove from heat regularly as you whisk.
ingredients: 200g fresh spinach, wilted and excess water squeezed out
For hollandaise: 3 egg yolks, 150g butter, lemon juice, salt, white pepper, pinch of cayenne
method: Make hollandaise: whisk yolks with lemon juice in a bowl over simmering water until pale; whisk in melted butter drop by drop until thick; season.
Poach eggs in simmering water with vinegar for 3 min.
Season spinach with salt and pepper; pile onto toasted muffins.
Place poached eggs on spinach.
Spoon hollandaise generously over each egg; dust with cayenne.

name: Mushroom Risotto
blurb: Arborio rice stirred slowly with wine and hot stock until each grain is enveloped in a silky, mushroom-scented sauce — risotto done with care.
tip: The final rest off the heat with butter stirred in — the mantecatura — is what transforms good risotto into great risotto.
ingredients: Olive oil, thyme, salt and pepper
method: Saute mushrooms in butter over high heat until golden; set aside.
In the same pan, soften onion in oil; add garlic and rice; stir 2 min until rice is translucent at edges.
Add wine; stir until absorbed.
Add hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each ladle to be absorbed before adding the next — about 20-22 min.
Fold in mushrooms and parmesan; stir in remaining butter; rest 2 min; garnish and serve.

name: Gnocchi al Pomodoro
blurb: Pillowy potato gnocchi tumbled in a bright, slow-cooked San Marzano tomato sauce and finished with torn basil and parmesan.
tip: Crushing the tomatoes by hand (not blending) keeps texture — a smooth sauce makes gnocchi feel heavy rather than light.
ingredients: 1 can (400g) San Marzano or whole plum tomatoes
method: Crush tomatoes by hand; saute garlic in olive oil until golden; add chilli.
Add tomatoes; season with salt; simmer 20 min until sauce is deep red and slightly reduced.
Cook gnocchi in boiling salted water until they float — about 2 min; drain.
Toss gnocchi directly into the tomato sauce; fold gently.
Serve immediately with torn basil and parmesan.

name: Vegetarian Shepherd's Pie
blurb: A deep dish of lentil and root vegetable stew topped with buttery mashed potato and baked until the crust is golden and crisp — proper cold-weather comfort.
tip: Roughing the mash surface with a fork creates peaks that catch heat and brown beautifully — a smooth surface stays pale.
ingredients: For mash: 4 large potatoes, 50g butter, warm milk, salt
method: Saute onion, carrot and celery until soft; add garlic and herbs; cook 1 min.
Stir in tomato paste; add lentils, peas and stock; simmer 10 min until slightly thick.
Transfer to a baking dish; season generously.
Boil potatoes; mash with butter and milk until smooth; season.
Spread mash over the filling; rough the top with a fork; bake at 200°C for 25 min until golden.

name: Ribollita (Tuscan Bread Soup)
blurb: Leftover bread and cannellini beans simmered with cavolo nero and vegetables into the thickest, most satisfying Tuscan soup.
tip: Ribollita means 'reboiled' — it is actually better re-heated, when the bread has fully absorbed the broth and become part of the soup.
ingredients: 200g cavolo nero or kale, roughly chopped
method: Saute onion, carrot and celery in olive oil until soft; add garlic and herbs.
Add tomatoes, beans and stock; simmer 20 min; add parmesan rind if using.
Add cavolo nero; cook 10 min more.
Stir in torn bread; cook until bread absorbs liquid and soup is very thick.
Serve in bowls with a generous drizzle of raw olive oil — best re-heated the next day.

name: Bruschetta al Pomodoro
blurb: Grilled bread rubbed with garlic and loaded with diced ripe tomato, fresh basil and a generous pour of good olive oil — Italy's greatest simple food.
tip: The garlic rub on hot toast is not optional — it melts into the bread and is the signature flavour of a proper bruschetta.
ingredients: 3 large ripe tomatoes, deseeded and diced
Optional: pinch of chilli flakes or balsamic glaze
method: Grill or toast bread slices until charred and crisp.
While hot, vigorously rub cut garlic over one side of each slice.
Toss diced tomato with olive oil, salt and basil; rest 5 min.
Spoon tomato generously onto garlic-rubbed bread.
Drizzle more olive oil; add pepper; serve immediately.

name: Cheese and Herb Scones
blurb: Buttery, flaky scones packed with mature cheddar and fresh chives — British afternoon baking at its most reliable and satisfying.
tip: The secret to risen scones is cold butter, cold milk and minimal mixing — warmth and overworking develop gluten and kill the lift.
method: Rub cold butter into flour until it resembles breadcrumbs; stir in baking powder, salt, mustard powder and pepper.
Mix in most of the cheese and the chives.
Add cold milk gradually; mix to a shaggy dough — do not overwork.
Pat to 2cm thickness; cut into rounds; place on a lined tray.
Brush with egg wash; scatter remaining cheese; bake at 220°C for 15-18 min until risen and golden.

name: Vegetable Crudites with Whipped Ricotta
blurb: A platter of seasonal raw vegetables arranged around a bowl of whipped ricotta with lemon and herbs — a light, elegant European appetiser.
tip: Season the ricotta assertively — it is meant to be the dip, not just a white backdrop, and underseasoned ricotta is bland.
ingredients: Zest and juice of half a lemon
Selection of vegetables: carrots, cucumber, radish, celery, bell pepper strips, fennel, endive leaves
Fresh dill and chives to garnish
method: Whip ricotta with lemon zest, juice, olive oil and garlic until smooth and creamy; season generously.
Spoon into a serving bowl; create a well in the centre; drizzle olive oil into the well.
Trim and cut all vegetables into dippable lengths or wedges.
Arrange vegetables around the dip in groups by colour and shape.
Scatter fresh herbs over the dip; serve chilled.

name: Huevos Rancheros
blurb: Fried eggs served on warm tortillas in a robust tomato and chilli salsa ranchera — the Mexican ranchero's breakfast that fuels a morning of work.
tip: Charring the tomatoes and chillies before blending gives the salsa ranchera a distinctive smokiness that raw-blended versions lack.
ingredients: For salsa ranchera: 3 tomatoes, 2 jalapeños, 1/2 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin
Fresh coriander and lime to serve
method: Char tomatoes, jalapeños and onion under a grill until blistered; blend with garlic and cumin; season.
Fry salsa in a little oil 5 min until it deepens in colour; keep warm.
Warm tortillas in a dry pan; fry eggs sunny side up.
Place two tortillas on each plate; spoon salsa over each; set a fried egg on top.
Add beans; drizzle crema; scatter coriander; squeeze lime.

name: Chilaquiles Verdes
blurb: Stale tortilla chips simmered briefly in a bright tomatillo salsa verde until they soften and absorb the sauce — served with eggs and crema.
tip: The chips should be just barely softened — remove from heat 30 seconds before they look done, as carryover heat finishes them.
method: Warm salsa verde with stock in a wide pan until simmering.
Add tortilla chips all at once; fold gently until chips are coated and beginning to soften — about 2-3 min; do not stir too much.
Plate immediately while the chips still have some texture.
Top with fried or poached egg, crema, cheese and onion.
Garnish with coriander and a wedge of lime.

name: Molletes with Refried Beans and Pico
blurb: Toasted bolillo rolls spread with refried beans and melted cheese, topped with fresh pico de gallo — Mexico City's beloved bread-and-beans breakfast.
tip: Warm the beans properly before spreading — cold refried beans on toast taste dense and pasty; warm beans are creamy and loose.
ingredients: For pico de gallo: 2 tomatoes, 1/4 onion, 1 jalapeño, coriander, lime juice, salt
method: Make pico: finely dice tomatoes, onion and jalapeño; toss with coriander, lime juice and salt; rest 10 min.
Toast rolls cut-side down in a dry pan or oven until golden.
Spread warm refried beans generously on each half.
Scatter cheese over the beans; grill until bubbling.
Top with a generous spoonful of pico de gallo; serve immediately.

name: Tamales de Elote (Sweet Corn Tamales)
blurb: Soft, slightly sweet corn dough steamed in corn husks — the tamale in its most basic and most honest form.
tip: The dough is ready when a small ball floats in a glass of cold water — this is the traditional Mexican freshness test.
ingredients: 2 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels
Warm water or broth to adjust consistency
Corn husks, soaked in warm water 30 min to soften
method: Blend corn kernels to a rough paste.
Beat butter until fluffy; add masa harina, sugar, baking powder and salt; mix in corn paste.
Add warm broth or water to form a soft, spreadable dough.
Spread 2 tbsp dough on a soaked husk; fold sides in, fold bottom up.
Stand tamales upright in a steamer; steam 50-60 min until dough pulls cleanly from the husk.

name: Avocado Tostada with Black Beans
blurb: A crisp, flat fried tortilla topped with refried black beans, smashed avocado, pickled jalapeños and crumbled cheese — the street-food tostada.
tip: Build and eat tostadas immediately — they are designed to be crispy and will soften within minutes of topping.
ingredients: 4 corn tortillas, fried flat until crisp
1 cup black beans, cooked and mashed
1/4 cup queso fresco or feta, crumbled
method: Fry tortillas flat in oil until completely crisp; drain on paper.
Season mashed black beans with cumin and salt; warm gently.
Season smashed avocado with lime juice and salt.
Spread beans on each tostada; add avocado; add cabbage.
Top with jalapeños, cheese, crema and coriander.

name: Enfrijoladas
blurb: Corn tortillas dipped in a thick, silky black bean sauce and folded with cheese inside — Mexico's humbler, earthier cousin to enchiladas.
tip: The bean sauce should coat the back of a spoon thickly — too thin and it soaks the tortilla into mush within seconds.
ingredients: 1/2 cup crumbled queso fresco or feta
Sour cream and fresh coriander to serve
method: Blend black beans with chipotle, garlic and onion, adding broth to reach a thick, pourable sauce; warm in a pan.
Briefly fry tortillas in oil 20 seconds each side to soften; drain.
Dip each tortilla in the warm bean sauce to coat; fold in half with a pinch of cheese inside.
Arrange two per plate; spoon more sauce over; add remaining cheese.
Serve with sour cream and coriander.

name: Black Bean Quesadilla
blurb: Flour tortillas filled with black beans, melted cheese and poblano pepper, pressed until crispy gold on the outside and gooey within.
tip: Medium heat is essential — too hot and the tortilla burns before the cheese melts; too low and it dries out rather than crisping.
ingredients: 1 poblano or green pepper, roasted and sliced
Butter or oil for the pan
Sour cream and guacamole to serve
method: Season black beans with cumin and smoked paprika.
Lay a tortilla flat; scatter beans, cheese and pepper strips on one half; fold over.
Heat a little butter in a flat pan over medium heat.
Cook quesadilla 2-3 min each side, pressing gently, until both sides are golden and cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges; serve with sour cream and guacamole.

name: Pozole Verde (Green Hominy Soup)
blurb: A soul-warming green stew of hominy, tomatillos and pumpkin seeds, served with a feast of toppings — Mexico's great ritual soup.
tip: Frying the green paste in oil before adding liquid is the key step — it transforms a raw, sharp blend into a deep, complex broth base.
ingredients: For green broth: 300g tomatillos, 1/2 cup pumpkin seeds toasted, 2 jalapeños, 2 garlic cloves, 1/4 onion, handful of epazote or coriander
Toppings: shredded cabbage, sliced radish, dried oregano, chilli flakes, lime, tostadas
method: Blend tomatillos, pumpkin seeds, jalapeños, garlic, onion and herbs with a little water to a smooth green paste.
Fry paste in hot oil 5 min, stirring constantly, until deep green and fragrant.
Add hominy and stock; simmer 25 min until hominy is tender and broth is rich.
Taste and season; adjust heat.
Ladle into deep bowls; set out all toppings for the table to add themselves.

name: Enchiladas Verdes
blurb: Corn tortillas rolled around a cheese and bean filling, nestled in tomatillo salsa verde and baked until the sauce bubbles.
tip: Softening the tortillas in oil before rolling prevents them from cracking and breaking when you fold them around the filling.
ingredients: 1 cup black beans or pinto beans, cooked
method: Briefly fry tortillas in oil to soften; do not crisp.
Mix beans with half the cheese; roll a spoonful inside each tortilla; place seam-down in a baking dish.
Pour salsa verde over to cover; scatter remaining cheese on top.
Bake at 190°C for 20 min until sauce is bubbling.
Drizzle crema; scatter queso fresco, coriander and onion; serve from the dish.

name: Calabacitas
blurb: A Mexican summer squash saute with corn, poblano and cheese — one of the most elemental and beloved side dishes in the Mexican kitchen.
tip: Pull the pan from heat as soon as you add the cheese — you want it to melt softly into the vegetables, not fry and become rubbery.
method: Melt butter; saute onion and poblano 5 min until soft; add garlic.
Add courgette and cook 8 min, stirring occasionally, until just tender.
Stir in corn; cook 3 min; season with salt, pepper and oregano.
Fold in cheese cubes; remove from heat and let cheese soften from the residual heat.
Garnish with epazote or coriander; serve as a side or over rice.

name: Fideo Seco (Dry Vermicelli)
blurb: Thin vermicelli pasta toasted in a pan then cooked in tomato broth until all the liquid absorbs — a comforting Mexican pasta dish that is deeply savoury.
tip: Toasting the dry noodles until truly golden is the defining step — under-toasted fideo tastes like plain pasta; properly toasted fideo is nutty and complex.
ingredients: 200g fideo noodles or thin vermicelli, broken
Crema, avocado and lime to serve
method: Blend tomatoes, chipotle, garlic and onion to a smooth sauce.
Toast dry fideo in oil over medium heat, stirring constantly, until golden — about 4-5 min; do not burn.
Pour blended tomato sauce into the pan — it will sizzle dramatically; stir.
Add stock; bring to a boil; reduce to a simmer; cook uncovered until liquid fully absorbs.
Serve with crema drizzled over, avocado slices and lime.

name: Guacamole and Totopos
blurb: Hand-mashed avocado with onion, chilli, coriander and lime — made fresh in a molcajete and eaten with crisp tortilla chips.
tip: Pressing a piece of cling film directly onto the surface of leftover guacamole — not over the bowl — is the only method that truly delays browning.
ingredients: 1/2 small white onion, very finely minced
method: Grind onion and chilli to a paste in a molcajete (or use a bowl and fork).
Add avocado; mash roughly — texture should be chunky, not smooth.
Fold in coriander; squeeze in lime juice; season with salt.
Taste and adjust chilli and lime.
Serve immediately with totopos — guacamole begins to oxidise within 30 min.

name: Churros with Chocolate Dipping Sauce
blurb: Crispy, golden fried dough coated in cinnamon sugar, served with a thick drinking-chocolate dip — the street-fair sweet of the Spanish-speaking world.
tip: Pipe churros directly into the oil from a piping bag — scissors in your other hand cut each one cleanly at the right length.
ingredients: For coating: 1/2 cup sugar + 1 tsp cinnamon
For dip: 150ml cream, 80g dark chocolate (70%), pinch of chilli
method: Bring water, salt and sugar to a boil; remove from heat; beat in flour to a smooth, stiff dough.
Cool slightly; pipe into hot oil (175°C) through a star nozzle in 12cm lengths; fry 3-4 min until golden.
Drain; immediately roll in cinnamon sugar.
Make dip: heat cream; pour over chopped chocolate; stir in chilli; stir until smooth.
Serve churros alongside the chocolate dipping sauce.

name: Pepino con Limón y Chile (Cucumber Snack)
blurb: Cucumber spears dressed with lime juice, chilli powder and salt — Mexico's purest, most refreshing street snack that needs no recipe, only quality.
tip: Tajin (a blend of chilli, lime and salt) is the ideal seasoning if you can find it — it is pre-balanced and requires no adjustment.
ingredients: 1 tsp chilli powder (Tajin or pure ancho chilli)
Optional: jicama spears, mango slices or watermelon to add variety
method: Cut cucumbers into long spears or rounds.
Arrange on a plate or in a cup.
Squeeze lime juice generously over all the pieces.
Dust with chilli powder and salt flakes.
Serve immediately and eat with your hands.

name: Msemen (Moroccan Layered Flatbread)
blurb: Flaky, laminated Moroccan griddle bread folded with butter and semolina — eaten warm with honey and argan oil for a quintessential Marrakchi morning.
tip: The double folding and laminating step is what creates the characteristic flaky layers — skipping it produces a dense flatbread.
ingredients: 3 tbsp melted butter and 3 tbsp vegetable oil for laminating
Honey and argan oil to serve
method: Mix flour, semolina, salt, sugar and yeast; add warm water to make a smooth, elastic dough; knead 10 min; rest 30 min.
Divide into balls; flatten each thin; brush with butter-oil mix; sprinkle semolina; fold in thirds then thirds again to form a square.
Rest 5 min; flatten each square thin again.
Cook on a dry griddle 3-4 min per side until golden and slightly puffed.
Drizzle honey and argan oil; serve warm.

name: Baghrir (Thousand-Hole Pancakes)
blurb: Semolina pancakes riddled with a honeycomb of holes, cooked only on one side, and served with a warm butter-and-honey dipping sauce.
tip: Cook on one side only — the holes form as steam rises through the batter, and flipping collapses them and ruins the texture.
ingredients: For sauce: 3 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp honey warmed together
method: Blend all batter ingredients until completely smooth; rest 15 min until slightly foamy.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour a ladle of batter; cook on one side only — do not flip; holes will form on the surface as it cooks.
Remove when the surface is fully set and no wet batter remains.
Dip each pancake in warm butter-honey sauce before each bite.

name: Sfenj (Moroccan Doughnuts)
blurb: Airy, yeasted Moroccan ring doughnuts fried golden and rolled in sugar — sold by street vendors in the early morning across the Maghreb.
tip: The dough should be sticky and loose — a stiffer dough produces dense, bready doughnuts rather than the light, airy sfenj.
ingredients: Warm water (approx 200ml) to make a sticky dough
method: Dissolve yeast in warm water; combine with flour, salt and sugar; beat to a sticky, loose dough; do not add more flour.
Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled and bubbly.
Wet hands; take a ball of dough; poke a hole through the centre; stretch into a ring.
Deep fry at 175°C until golden on both sides — 3-4 min total.
Drain briefly; roll in sugar; eat warm.

name: Sellou (Roasted Flour Energy Bite)
blurb: A Moroccan sweet of dry-roasted flour, sesame, almonds and honey — no baking needed, shaped into pyramids, eaten especially during Ramadan.
tip: Roasting the flour until genuinely golden (not just warm) is what gives sellou its distinctive nutty, toasty depth.
ingredients: 1/2 cup almonds, toasted and coarsely ground
method: Dry-roast flour in a pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, until golden and nutty — about 20 min; cool.
Mix roasted flour with ground almonds, sesame, cinnamon, anise, ginger and salt.
Melt butter into honey; pour over dry mixture; stir until it clumps.
Shape into small pyramids or balls; dust with icing sugar.
Serve at room temperature; store in an airtight tin for up to two weeks.

name: Couscous Tfaya (Caramelised Onion Couscous)
blurb: A mound of steamed couscous crowned with the Moroccan 'tfaya' — a silky, caramelised onion and raisin sauce scented with ras el hanout and cinnamon.
tip: Low and slow is the only way to caramelise onions properly — the 30-minute cook time is not optional and cannot be rushed on high heat.
ingredients: Fried almonds and hard-boiled egg to garnish
method: Saute onions in oil on low heat for 25-30 min until deeply caramelised and sticky.
Add spices, saffron, raisins, honey and water; cook 10 min until thick and jammy.
Steam couscous with butter and salt until fluffy and light.
Mound couscous on a serving platter; make a well in the centre.
Pour tfaya into the well; garnish with fried almonds and egg slices; serve.

name: Loubia (White Bean Stew)
blurb: Creamy cannellini beans in a deeply spiced tomato and cumin broth — a staple of the Moroccan and Algerian table, eaten with crusty khobz bread.
tip: Mashing a quarter of the beans into the broth creates the thick, velvety texture that distinguishes loubia from a watery bean soup.
ingredients: Fresh parsley and lemon to serve
method: Saute onion in olive oil until golden; add garlic, cumin and paprika; fry 1 min.
Add tomatoes, harissa and chilli; simmer 10 min.
Add beans and enough water to just cover; simmer 15 min until broth is rich.
Mash a few beans against the side of the pan to thicken.
Drizzle olive oil; scatter parsley; serve with a wedge of lemon and bread.

name: Chermoula Salad
blurb: A vibrant salad dressed in chermoula — Morocco's signature herb and spice marinade of coriander, cumin and lemon — tossed with roasted vegetables.
tip: Chermoula is better when the vegetables are still warm — the heat opens the surface and allows the marinade to soak in rather than just sitting on top.
ingredients: For chermoula: 1 bunch coriander, 4 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp chilli, juice of 1 lemon, 4 tbsp olive oil
method: Blend chermoula ingredients to a coarse, herb-flecked paste; season with salt.
Slice roasted vegetables and arrange on a platter.
Spoon chermoula generously over while vegetables are still warm.
Rest 10 min for the dressing to penetrate.
Serve at room temperature with crusty bread.

name: Bastilla au Légumes (Vegetable Pastry Pie)
blurb: A Moroccan filo pie layered with almonds, spiced vegetables and scrambled egg, dusted with cinnamon and icing sugar — savoury and sweet in one dramatic dish.
tip: The sweet-savoury contrast of icing sugar and cinnamon on top is not decorative — it is essential to bastilla's flavour identity.
ingredients: 2 courgettes and 1 carrot, diced and cooked
1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ginger, 1/4 tsp pepper
Icing sugar and cinnamon to dust top
method: Fry onion; add vegetables and spices; cook until dry; season.
Scramble eggs gently into the vegetable mix; cool.
Line a round tin with buttered filo sheets, overlapping; fill with almond layer then vegetable layer.
Fold overhanging pastry over; top with two more buttered sheets.
Bake 30 min at 190°C until golden; invert; dust with icing sugar and cinnamon pattern.

name: Loubia Tagine with Preserved Lemon
blurb: Green beans simmered in a fragrant tomato and preserved lemon tagine sauce — the everyday Moroccan vegetable dish at its most straightforward.
tip: Moroccan tagine vegetables are intentionally cooked until very soft — al dente is not the goal here; tenderness and flavour absorption are.
ingredients: 400g green beans or runner beans, trimmed
1/2 preserved lemon, flesh removed and rind finely diced
method: Saute onion in oil until soft; add garlic and spices; fry 1 min.
Add tomatoes and preserved lemon; cook 5 min until tomatoes break down.
Add beans and 1/2 cup water; cover and simmer 20-25 min until beans are very tender.
The sauce should be thick and coating; uncover last 5 min if too watery.
Scatter herbs; drizzle raw olive oil; serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Briouats (Fried Filo Triangles)
blurb: Crispy triangular filo pastries stuffed with a fragrant almond, honey and cinnamon filling — a Moroccan celebratory sweet that is impossible to eat just one of.
tip: Seal the edges with melted butter as you fold — any opening will cause the triangles to burst and fill the oil with almonds.
ingredients: 8 sheets filo pastry, cut into strips
Extra honey and sesame seeds to finish
method: Mix ground almonds with honey, orange blossom water, cinnamon and ginger to a paste.
Place a teaspoon of filling at the base of a filo strip; fold into a triangle, sealing with melted butter; repeat.
Deep fry at 170°C until golden — 2-3 min; drain.
While hot, drizzle with honey and scatter sesame seeds.
Serve warm or at room temperature; store in an airtight tin.

name: Khobz (Moroccan Round Bread)
blurb: Morocco's everyday round, slightly domed bread — baked in a communal oven or home oven until the crust is golden and the crumb is soft and chewy.
tip: The tap test is more reliable than timing — every oven differs, and a hollow sound tells you the bread is done even if the colour seems light.
method: Combine flour, yeast, salt and sugar; add oil and enough warm water to form a smooth, elastic dough.
Knead 10 min; rest 1 hr until doubled.
Divide into two rounds; shape into flat discs; dust with semolina.
Rest 20 min; score tops with a knife.
Bake at 220°C for 20-25 min until golden; tap the base — it should sound hollow.

name: Maakouda (Potato Fritter)
blurb: Golden potato cakes flavoured with cumin, coriander and harissa, fried crisp on the outside — Tunisia's beloved street fritter, eaten in a sandwich or alone.
tip: Chilling the shaped patties before frying is important — cold potato holds together in the oil; warm potato breaks apart.
method: Combine mashed potato with egg, garlic, cumin, coriander, harissa, parsley, salt and pepper.
Shape into round patties about 1cm thick; refrigerate 10 min to firm.
Shallow fry in hot oil 3-4 min each side until deep golden.
Drain on paper; serve hot with harissa, olives or inside crusty bread.
They will hold their shape better if not touched for the first 2 min of frying.

name: Kaab el Ghazal (Gazelle Horns)
blurb: Elegant crescent-shaped Moroccan cookies filled with almond paste and orange blossom — the pastry that has graced every Moroccan celebration table for centuries.
tip: Kaab el ghazal should be pale — over-baking dries out the almond paste and loses the soft, marzipan-like interior that defines them.
ingredients: For pastry: 2 cups flour, 4 tbsp butter, pinch of salt, orange blossom water to bind
For filling: 2 cups ground almonds, 1/2 cup icing sugar, 1 tbsp orange blossom water, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tbsp butter
method: Mix almond filling ingredients to a smooth paste; form into thin finger-shaped logs.
Make pastry by rubbing butter into flour; add orange blossom water to form a pliable dough; rest 30 min.
Roll pastry thin; place almond log on one edge; roll to encase; seal and curve into a crescent.
Bake at 180°C for 12-15 min — they should be barely golden, not brown.
Cool; dust generously with icing sugar.

name: Couscous with Seven Vegetables (Algerian)
blurb: A magnificent Algerian couscous prepared with seven symbolic vegetables in a deep, saffron-spiced broth — a Friday dish and a festive one.
tip: Steaming the couscous above the broth rather than just hydrating it with boiling water gives it an incomparably lighter texture.
ingredients: 1 tsp ras el hanout, 1/4 tsp saffron, 1 tsp cinnamon
